Included in betraying their trusts is ghulul (misappropriation) from the spoils of war, meaning stealing from them, and betraying everything that people entrust, whether wealth, family, or secrets, and everything in which they have been required to worship [Allah].

It has been narrated concerning the revelation of the verse something of what we have mentioned. The wording of the verse is general and encompasses that and other things.

Among that is what Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, who said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged Qurayzah and commanded them to come down under the judgment of Sa'd. Qurayzah consulted Abu Lubabah about coming down under the judgment of Sa'd, and Abu Lubabah's family and property were among them. So he gestured toward his throat, meaning that it would be slaughter. Abu Lubabah said: "My feet did not move until I knew that I had betrayed Allah and His Messenger." Then he swore that he would not taste food until he died or Allah accepted his repentance.

He went to the mosque and tied himself to a pillar (sariyah). He remained for days until he would collapse unconscious from exhaustion. Then Allah revealed his repentance, and he swore that none would untie him except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his own hand. So he (ﷺ) untied him, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I had vowed to strip myself of my wealth as charity." He (ﷺ) said: "A third is sufficient for you to give in charity."

Some of the exegetes said: This occasion indicates the permissibility of openly showing distress over a sin, and of exhausting and reproaching oneself, because the Prophet (ﷺ) did not disapprove of Abu Lubabah.

It also indicates that it is recommended to follow a sin with charity, and because he, peace be upon him, said: "A third of your wealth is sufficient for you," this is in line with His saying in Hud: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds﴾ [Hud: 114].

In His saying: ﴿while you know﴾ there is evidence that the sin of one who knows is greater than that of others, because the meaning is: while you know the consequence of that and its ruin.

Al-Razi said: Since the motive for proceeding to betrayal is the love of wealth and children, Allah, exalted is He, alerted that it is obligatory for the intelligent person to guard against the harm arising from that love, so He said:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 28:

(p-2980) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial (fitnah), and that with Allah is a great reward.﴾

﴿And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial (fitnah)﴾ That is: a test from Allah, by which He tries you, to see whether you fall into betrayal through them, or whether you leave for them the response to Allah and His Messenger, or whether you are not diverted by them from His remembrance and do not trade them for Him.

They are called (fitnah) in consideration of what befalls a person from being tested through them. It is also permissible that by (fitnah) is meant sin or punishment, since they are the cause of falling into that.

Al-Hakim said: Allah has commanded knowledge of this, and the way to knowing it is reflection upon their conditions and their passing away, the scarcity of benefit from them, the abundance of harm, and that a person may disobey Allah because of them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that with Allah is a great reward﴾ means: for the one who prefers His pleasure over the gathering of wealth and the love of children, so that he does not expose himself to ruin on their account.

The warning against being tested by them has come explicitly, together with severe intimidation, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers.﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9] It has been said: this verse is among what was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah, and what slipped from him on account of his wealth and his child.

When Allah, exalted is He, had warned, regarding what preceded, about the trial by wealth and children, He gave good tidings to whoever fears Him in being tempted by them and in other matters, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 29:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[29] ﴿O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqan) and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾

(p-2981) Al-Mahayimi said: He, exalted is He, indicated that whoever abandons betrayal and responds to Allah will not fear for his family, his wealth, or his honor, meaning: just as Abu Lubaba feared.

For whoever fears Him, exalted is He, no one will dare to encroach upon his family and his domain, because he is granted a furqan by which he is distinguished from the rest of people in awe and honor. End of quote.

It was said: ﴿furqan﴾ means victory, because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between disbelief, by humiliating its party, and Islam, by exalting its people.

From this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿the Day of the Furqan﴾ [al-Anfal: 41]. It was also said: clarity and manifestation that makes your affair famous, and spreads your renown and your traces throughout the regions of the earth, from their saying: "I spent the night doing such-and-such until the furqan shone," meaning: the dawn rose.

It was said: a separation between truth and falsehood, and a bringing out from doubts, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will make for you a light by which you walk, and will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Hadid: 28]

Al-furqan, like al-farq, is a verbal noun from (faraqa), meaning he separated one thing from another, whether by what the eye perceives or by what insight perceives. However, al-furqan is more eloquent, because it is used for distinguishing between truth and falsehood, and between proof and doubt.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[30] ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots. And Allah is the best of planners.﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots. And Allah is the best of planners.﴾

When Allah, exalted is He, reminded the believers of His favours upon them by His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And remember when you were few﴾ [al-Anfal: 26], He reminded the Prophet (ﷺ) of His favour upon him in particular, in protecting him from the plotting of Quraysh against him, so that he would thank Him, exalted is He, for his deliverance from their plot and his triumph over them. This occurred because "when the Ansar embraced Islam, and the light of Islam began to spread, Quraysh feared that his affair would grow greatly, so they gathered in the Dar al-Nadwa (it is a house built by Qusayy ibn Kilab to settle disputes among Quraysh, then it became a place for their consultation; it is now the place of al-Hanafi. An-nadwah is the assembly of the people, and nada the place means the people gathered in it, and from it comes an-nadi (the assembly)) to consult about his affair (ﷺ)."

Abu al-Bukhturi ibn Hisham said: "My opinion is that you should imprison him in a room, bind his shackles, and seal his door, except for a small opening through which you pass him his food and drink, and wait for him to meet the fate of mortals."

This is what is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿to confine you﴾, meaning to imprison and bind you, because whoever holds something back and ties it down has made it fixed, unable to move from it.

Then a Najdi shaykh who had joined them objected to this opinion, saying: "What a bad opinion! Someone will come to you from his people to fight you and free him from your hands!" Then Hisham ibn Amr said: "My opinion is that you should load him onto his camel and expel him from among you, so that what he has done will no longer trouble you, and you will be at rest."

This is what is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or expel you﴾, meaning from Makkah. Then the Najdi objected again, saying: "What a bad opinion! He will corrupt another people besides you and fight you with them." Then Abu Jahl—may Allah curse him—said: "I see that you should take from every clan a young man and give him a sword, and they should strike him with the blow of a single man, so his blood will be scattered among the tribes, and the Banu Hashim will not be able to fight all of Quraysh. If they demand the blood-money, we will pay it and be at rest." This is what Allah, exalted is He, mentioned by His saying: ﴿or kill you﴾.

Then the accursed Najdi said: "This young man has spoken the truth; he is the best of you in opinion." So they dispersed upon the opinion of Abu Jahl, unanimously agreed upon killing him. Then Jibril, peace be upon him, informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and commanded him not to sleep in his bed, and Allah permitted him to emigrate. So he commanded Ali, and he slept in his bed, and said to him: "Wrap yourself in my cloak, for nothing you dislike will reach you."

(p-2983) Then the Prophet (ﷺ) went out, took a handful of dust, and Allah blinded their sight to him. He began scattering the dust over their heads while reciting: ﴿Ya-Sin﴾ [Ya-Sin: 1] ﴿By the wise Qur'an﴾ [Ya-Sin: 2] up to His saying ﴿so they do not see﴾ [Ya-Sin: 9].

He proceeded with Abu Bakr to the cave, and the polytheists spent the night guarding Ali, thinking he was the Prophet. When they rose in the morning, they went to him to kill him, and they saw Ali, and said: "Where is your companion?" He said: "I do not know!" So they followed his trail, and when they reached the cave, they saw the spider's web over its entrance, and said: "Had he entered it, the spider's web would not remain intact." Allah frustrated their effort and nullified their plot.

Then he (ﷺ) remained in it for three days, then went out to Madinah."

This was narrated from Ibn Abbas through several chains, in the works of Ibn Ishaq, Imam Ahmad, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi; the narrations of some of them overlap with others.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah plots﴾ means: He arranges what nullifies their plot. His saying: ﴿And Allah is the best of planners﴾ means: the most powerful in effect, as said by al-Mahayimi. He also noted, regarding the connection of this verse with what precedes it, that this indicates that the God-conscious person, just as Allah makes for him a criterion that protects him from being attacked in his family, wealth and honour, outwardly protects him from the plot of one who plots against him; rather, He plots on his behalf against his plotter. End of quote.

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed of the disbelief, arrogance and defiance of Quraysh, and their false claims upon hearing His verses, by His saying:

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[31] ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the legends of the former peoples."﴾

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard"﴾ — i.e., (they say) "the like of this." ﴿"If we wished, we could say the like of this"﴾ — i.e., of what is recited.

This is the utmost in obstinate arrogance and the extreme of stubbornness.

How could it not be so? For if they were able to produce anything of that kind, what would have prevented them from willing it? They were challenged more than once to produce a surah like it, they were rebuked for their inability, and they tasted the bitterest of humiliation because of it. Then they were confronted with the sword, and yet they did not contend with it (i.e., the Qur'an) with anything else, despite their extreme pride and their disdain at being overcome, especially in the field of eloquence (bayan) in which they were the masters, holding its reins, and their utmost delight in it.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿"This is nothing but the legends of the former peoples"﴾ — i.e., what they inscribed and wrote of tales. It has been said: "asatir" has no singular; and it has been said: it is a plural, of "asṭur," "suṭūr," and "asṭār," the plurals of "saṭr" (line) and "ahadith" (tales). The basic meaning of "saṭr" is a line and writing. It is said: "saṭara" means "he wrote," and it is also applied to a row of a thing, such as of a book or of trees. Thus in al-Qamus and its commentary.

It has been narrated that the one who said this was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith from Kildah, and that he had gone to the lands of Persia and came back with a copy of the stories of Rustam and Isfandiyar. When he returned, he found that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been sent by Allah and was reciting to the people what Allah, exalted is He, had related of the tales of past generations.

He said: "If you wished, you could say the like of this." He claimed that it was similar to what he had gleaned. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) rose from a gathering, al-Nadr would sit in his place and narrate to them from what he had picked up. Then he would say: "By Allah! Which of us is better at storytelling, I or Muhammad?"

Allah enabled [the Muslims] to overcome him on the Day of Badr; al-Miqdad captured him, then the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered him, and his neck was struck.

His attribution of this statement to all of them (i.e., the disbelievers) is either because the rest were content with it, or because its speaker was a great and followed figure. The accursed one was their storyteller, who taught them falsehood, led them to it, and deceived them with such empty babble.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[32] ﴿And when they said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."﴾

This is an eloquent form of denial, for they regarded the truth of the Qur'an as impossible, and therefore they tied to it a request for a punishment that no sensible person would ask for; had it been possible, they would have fled from tying it to that condition.

The meaning is: if this Qur'an is indeed a truth sent down, then punish us for denying it with sijjil (baked clay stones), as You did to the people of the Elephant, or with some other punishment.

In their description of it as (the truth) and their making it from Allah, there is a mocking of the one who says so, whether the Prophet or the believers. The benefit of the definite article here is to indicate that what is conditioned upon is its being the truth in the manner that he ﷺ claims it, namely that it is a revelation sent down, not the truth absolutely, since they allowed that it might correspond to reality while not being sent down, like the fables of the ancients. Thus the definite article is for reference to a known thing.

And: (rain down, amtir) is a metaphor or figurative usage (meaning: send down, anzil).

Al-Zamakhshari said: The use of "imtar" (raining) for punishment is frequent. If you ask: what is the benefit of His words "from the sky," since raining only comes from it? I say: it is as if it was intended to say: "rain down upon us sijjil," and that is the stones marked for punishment; so "stones from the sky" was placed in the position of "sijjil," just as you say: "he poured upon him masrudah of iron," meaning a coat of mail.

His words "with a painful punishment" mean: other than the aforementioned rain, or it is the general following the specific.

It is related from Mu'awiyah that he said to a man from Saba': "How ignorant your people were when they made a woman their king!" He replied: "Your people are more ignorant than my people! They said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he invited them to the truth: 'If this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones,' and they did not say: 'If this is indeed the truth, then guide us to it.'"

That is: the one which is best for them. But because of the extreme ignorance, obstinacy and stubbornness, they sought to hasten the outcome against themselves and wanted the punishment brought forward, as in His words: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment, and had there not been a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them, and it will surely come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 53], ﴿And they said: "Our Lord, hasten for us our portion before the Day of Reckoning"﴾ [Sad: 16], and His words: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is to befall﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1], ﴿for the disbelievers; none can avert it﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 2], ﴿from Allah, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 3]. Likewise the foolish among the former nations said, as the people of Shu'ayb said to him: ﴿So cause fragments of the sky to fall upon us, if you are of the truthful﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 187].

(p-2986) It is related from 'Ata', Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that the one who said this was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, the companion of the earlier statement.

'Ata' said: About al-Nadr there were revealed some ten-odd verses, and what he asked for in punishment befell him on the Day of Badr.

Al-Bukhari related from Anas that the one who said this was Abu Jahl.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Buraydah, who said: I saw 'Amr ibn al-'As standing on a horse on the Day of Uhud, saying: "O Allah, if what Muhammad says is true, then swallow me and my horse up."

And His words, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 33:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[33] ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾

﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ is an explanation of the reason for their being given respite and for the non-answering of their supplication.

The lam here is for emphasizing the negation, and it indicates that punishing them while the Prophet is among them is not consistent with wisdom, because it is His (exalted is He) sunnah and the requirement of His wisdom that He not punish a nation while its Prophet is in their midst. For if the punishment descended upon their place, it would strike everyone who was in it. There is also an indication in this that they are kept under watch for punishment once he (ﷺ) emigrates from them.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, the scholars have mentioned three aspects regarding it:

The first: that what is meant is the seeking of forgiveness by those among them who remained, from the weak Muslims.

Al-Tibi said: "This aspect is more eloquent, because it indicates that the seeking of forgiveness by others is something by which punishment is averted from such disbelievers."

(p-2987) The second: that what is meant by it is the supplication of the disbelievers for forgiveness, and their saying "Ghufranaka" (Your forgiveness) during their circumambulation of the House, as narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Thus the mere request of forgiveness from Him, exalted is He, prevents His punishment, even if it comes from disbelievers.

The third: that what is meant by seeking forgiveness is repentance and turning away from all that they are upon of disbelief and other things. In this case the condition is negated, and it is affirmed in the first two aspects.

Al-Qashani said: "Punishment is the blaze and effect of anger, so it occurs only from the anger of the Prophet, or from the anger of Allah caused by the sins of the nation. The Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace, was the embodiment of mercy, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya: 107]. For this reason, when they broke his front tooth, he said: "O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know," and he did not become angry as Nuh, upon him peace, became angry and said: ﴿And Nuh said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers a dwelling-place﴾ [Nuh: 26].

Thus his presence among them prevents the descent of punishment, and likewise the presence of seeking forgiveness, for the primary cause of punishment is the existence of sin, and seeking forgiveness prevents sin from accumulating and persisting; rather, it necessitates its removal, so it does not cause the anger of Allah. So long as seeking forgiveness is among them, they will not be punished." End of quotation.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah sent down to me two securities for my nation: ﴿And Allah would not punish them﴾ up to the end of the verse. When I pass away, I will leave among them the seeking of forgiveness until the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Kathir said: What supports this is what Imam Ahmad and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated, from Abu Sa'id that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Iblis said to his Lord: By Your might and majesty, I will not cease misguiding the children of Adam as long as their souls are within them. Allah said: By My might and majesty, I will not cease forgiving them so long as they seek My forgiveness."

(p-2988) Imam Ahmad narrated from Fadala ibn Ubayd, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The servant is safe from the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so long as he seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

Then He, exalted is He, explained that they were deserving of punishment were it not for the preventing factor mentioned previously, in His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[34] ﴿And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram?﴾ and the rest of the verse: ﴿And they were not its guardians. Its guardians are none but the righteous, but most of them do not know.﴾

﴿And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram⁠﴾ meaning: what is there for them in the absence of punishment from them, when their condition is barring [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram, just as they barred the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah? Among their barring of him was forcing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers into emigration (hijrah).

Al-Qashani said: That is, the non-descent of punishment is not because they do not deserve it in themselves; rather, they deserve it in their very essence, due to their obstruction and their barring of those who are prepared [for guidance], and the absence of goodness remaining in them. But what prevents it is your presence and the presence of the believers who seek forgiveness along with you among them.

Then he said: Know that contingent existence follows the predominant good, because necessary existence is pure good. Whatever its good outweighs its evil, it exists by its existence through the good suitability (al-munasabah al-khayriyyah). When evil prevails, the suitability does not remain, so its eradication and annihilation become necessary.

So as long as they were in the social form, the good among them was predominant, so they did not deserve destruction by punishment. But when they scattered, nothing remained of them but pure evil, so their destruction became obligatory, as occurred in the event of Badr.

From this the realization of the second meaning in His saying, exalted is He, becomes clear: ﴿And beware of a trial that will not strike those among you who have done wrong in particular⁠﴾ [al-Anfal: 25],

because the Sharia then prevails over the whole. End of quotation.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they were not its guardians⁠﴾ is a refutation of what they used to say: "We are the custodians of the House and the Sacred Precinct; we bar whom we wish and admit whom we wish." That is: they did not deserve the guardianship of His affair, because of their polytheism. ﴿Its guardians are none but the righteous⁠﴾ — that is, the righteous from polytheism — so it is for them to bar the corrupters. ﴿But most of them do not know⁠﴾ — that is, that they have no guardianship over it.

**On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[35] ﴿Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.﴾

﴿Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling﴾, meaning *taṣfīr* (whistling), ﴿and clapping﴾, meaning *taṣfīq* (clapping with the hands).

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that Ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, described their practice, and he whistled, inclined his cheek, and clapped his hands.

Also from Ibn Umar, he said: "They used to place their cheeks on the ground, whistle, and clap."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from Ibn Abbas that they used to circumambulate the House naked, whistling and clapping.

From Mujahid: they did this in order to confuse the Prophet ﷺ in his prayer.

al-Zuhri said: they used to mock the believers.

This clause may be coordinated with ﴿and they bar [people]﴾ [al-Anfal: 34], in which case it serves to confirm their deserving of the punishment; or with His words ﴿nor were they its guardians﴾ [al-Anfal: 34], in which case it serves to confirm that they did not deserve its guardianship.

al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, "What is the meaning of this statement?" I answer: it is similar to the words of al-Farazdaq:

*"I never feared that his gift would be black shackles or whips of ash-wood."*

The meaning is that he placed chains and whips in the position of a gift, and they placed whistling and clapping in the position of prayer.

They used to circumambulate the House naked, men and women, interlacing their fingers, whistling into them and clapping.

They did this whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited in his prayer, and they would confuse him.

*"I never feared"* means: "I never knew." *Adahim* is the plural of *adham*, which is the black snake; the Arabs use *al-adham* to mean the shackle, as in the story of al-Qabʿathra.

*al-Muhadrajah* means the whips. End of quotation.

﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve﴾, meaning in belief and in action. This implies that this act, which violates the sanctity of the House, is disbelief, because it treats the rites of Allah, Exalted is He, with contempt and mockery.

The punishment mentioned is what befell them on the day of Badr of killing and capture, as stated by more than one of the early generations (*salaf*), and as chosen by Ibn Jarir.

**Note:**

Ibn al-Qayyim, in *Ighathat al-Lahfan*, said: Those who draw near to Allah through whistling and clapping, and who mix these into the prayer, the recitation, and the remembrance of the people of prayer, are like these polytheists. Ibn Arafa and Ibn al-Anbari said: Whistling and clapping are not prayer, but Allah, Exalted is He, informed us that they put whistling and clapping in place of the prayer they had been commanded to perform, and this brought upon them grave burdens of sin. This is like your saying: "I visited him, and he made my estrangement my kindness," meaning he set estrangement in the place of kindness.

The point is that those who clap and whistle along with the reed-pipe, the *mizmar* (flute), or the like, share a resemblance with these people. Even if it is only an outward resemblance, they bear a portion of the blame in proportion to their imitation of them, even if they do not imitate them in all of their whistling and clapping. Allah, glorified is He, did not legislate clapping for men at the time of need during prayer, when some matter befalls them; rather, they were commanded to turn away from it to glorification (*tasbih*), lest they imitate women. How much more so, then, when they do it without any need, and join with it kinds of disobedience in speech and action. End of quotation.

Before this, he also said: Among the snares and traps of the enemy of Allah, with which he has deceived those whose share of knowledge, intellect, and religion is small, and with which he has caught the hearts of the ignorant and the falsifiers, is listening to whistling and clapping, and to singing with forbidden instruments, which turns hearts away from the Qur'an and makes them devoted to transgression and disobedience.

His shaykh, Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, said in one of his fatawa: As for adopting clapping, singing, striking tambourines, blowing pipes, and gathering for these things as a religion and a path to Allah and an act of worship, this is not from the religion of Islam, nor is it something their Prophet Muhammad ﷺ legislated for them, nor any of his successors, nor did any of the imams of the Muslims approve of it. Indeed, no one among the people of religion used to do this in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor in the time of his Companions, nor of their Followers in goodness (*tabi'un*), nor of the Followers of the Followers. Rather, none of the people of religion in the three best centuries, in the Hijaz, in al-Sham, in Yemen, in Iraq, in Khurasan, in the Maghrib, or in Egypt, gathered for this kind of listening. It was only innovated in Islam after the three generations. For this reason al-Shafi'i said, when he saw it: "I left in Baghdad something that the heretics (*zanadiqa*) invented, which they call *al-taghbir*, by which they turn people away from the Qur'an." Ahmad was asked about it and said: "I dislike it, it is an innovation." It was said: "Do you sit with them?" He said: "No!" Likewise, all the imams of the religion disliked it, and the great righteous shaykhs did not attend it. Thus did not attend it Ibrahim ibn Adham, al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, Ma'ruf al-Karkhi, Abu Sulayman al-Darani, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari, al-Sari al-Saqati, and their like.

Those shaykhs who did attend it, among the praiseworthy ones, abandoned it at the end of their matter. And the prominent shaykhs found fault with its practitioners, as Shaykh Abd al-Qadir, Shaykh Abu al-Bayan, and others among the shaykhs have mentioned. What Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with them, mentioned, that it is an innovation of the heretics, is the statement of an imam expert in the foundations of Islam. This listening was not desired or called to in origin except by one accused of heresy, such as Ibn al-Rawandi, al-Farabi, Ibn Sina, and their like.

Then he, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yes! Some people who have the aspiration and love, and who have a share in love, have attended it, because it stirs them, but they did not know its harm, nor did they recognize its outcome. Just as some jurists entered into kinds of the speech of the philosophers that oppose the religion of Islam, thinking it to be true and in agreement, but they did not know its harm, nor did they recognize its outcome. The upholding of the realities of religion in knowledge, speech, action, taste, and experience is not something that most people can accomplish independently. The comprehensive proof, rather, is holding fast to the Book and the Sunnah.

Then he, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Whoever has experience of the realities of religion, and of the states of the hearts, their knowledge, and their tastes, knows that listening to whistling and clapping brings no benefit or good to the heart unless within it there is harm greater than that benefit. It is to the spirit what wine is to the body: it does to souls greater than what the fervor of the cups does. Then he said: In sum, the believer must know that the Prophet ﷺ did not leave anything that brings one closer to Paradise without having mentioned it, nor anything that distances one from the Fire without having mentioned it. And if this listening were a benefit, Allah and His Messenger would have legislated it, for Allah says: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3], to the end of the verse.

And if the listener finds in it a benefit for his heart, but does not find any witness to it in the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger, he should not give it any attention. Just as the jurist, if he sees an analogy (*qiyas*) that the Book and the Sunnah do not support, does not give it any attention. End of quotation.

Some of this discussion has already preceded us at His words, Exalted is He: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152]. So let it be referred to there.

The discussion of the words of His, exalted is He:

[36] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. They will spend it; then it will be a regret for them; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered unto Hell.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. They will spend it; then it will be a regret for them; then they will be overcome.﴾ (p-2993) It was revealed concerning those among the polytheists who spent on fighting the Prophet ﷺ, and it explains the evil outcome of this spending. Al-Dahhak held that it refers to those among them who fed people at Badr, and they were twelve men from Quraysh, each of whom fed ten camels every day.

It is narrated from Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and others that it was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan and his spending of wealth at (Uhud) to fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Zuhri that when Quraysh suffered at the Battle of Badr and their remnant returned to Makkah, and Abu Sufyan returned with his caravan, some men of Quraysh whose fathers, sons and brothers had been struck down at Badr walked to Abu Sufyan and to those who had trade in that caravan, and they said: "O assembly of Quraysh, indeed Muhammad has wronged you and killed your best men. So help us with this wealth against his war, that perhaps we may obtain vengeance from him for those of ours who were struck down." And they did so. He said: It was concerning them, as has been mentioned from Ibn Abbas, that the verse was revealed. And the verse's inclusion of all of that is not hidden.

The lam in ﴿li-yasuddu[ā]﴾ is the lam of result (lam al-sayrurah), and it is permissible for it to be the lam of purpose (al-ta'lil), because their aim was to bar from what is in reality the way of Allah, even though it was not so in their belief.

The way of Allah (sabil Allah) is His path, which is His religion and following His Messenger. Since the relative clause contains the meaning of a condition, and the predicate functions as the consequent, which is: ﴿fa-sa-yunfiquna-ha﴾, the word (yunfiqun) is joined by the fa' (in the sense of a consequence). It may be a circumstantial clause (hal) or an apposition (badal) from (kafaru). In the consequent's containing the sense of informing and notification, there is a rebuke for the spending and a denunciation of it, as in His saying: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 53].

In the repetition of "spending" within the condition-like structure, there is an indication of the complete badness of the spending, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, whoever You cause to enter the Fire, You have disgraced him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 192], and the saying: "Whoever reaches al-Samman has reached the pasture." The meaning is: those who spend their wealth to extinguish the light of Allah and to bar [people] from following His Messenger ﷺ will soon know the evil outcome (p-2994) of that spending and its turning into the greatest loss, through killing and capture in this world, and punishment in the Hereafter. Al-Mutanabbi said:

*When generosity is not granted deliverance from harm, then praise is not acquired and wealth does not endure.*

(Here "harm" means reproach for benefaction.)

In making the very wealth become ﴿hasrah﴾, i.e., regret and grief—which is the outcome of its affair—there is hyperbole.

The meaning of "overcoming" in His saying ﴿then they will be overcome﴾ is the defeat upon which the matter settled, even though the war between them was a back-and-forth contest before that. If you say: the Muslims' victory preceded their grief in time, so why was it mentioned later? I say: the meaning is that they will be overcome in other occasions after that. Thus in (al-'Inayah).

Admonition:

Some of them said: The benefit of the verse is the gravity of assisting in disobedience to Allah the Exalted, and that spending in that is disobedience. Included in this is assisting oppressors in their movements of transgression and wrongdoing, and likewise selling weapons and horses to one who uses them to fight the Muslims.

﴿And those who disbelieve will be gathered unto Hell.﴾

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[37] ﴿So that Allah may separate the evil from the good, and put the evil on top of one another, pile it all up together, and then cast it into Hell. It is they who are the losers.﴾

﴿So that Allah may separate the evil from the good﴾: that is, the disbeliever from the believer, or corruption from righteousness. The lam (the particle of purpose "so that") is connected to ﴿they will be gathered﴾ [al-Anfal: 36], or to ﴿they will be overcome﴾ [al-Anfal: 36], or to what the polytheists spent in opposition to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), of what the Muslims spent in supporting him. The lam is connected to His words: ﴿then it will become an anguish for them﴾ [al-Anfal: 36].

﴿and put the evil on top of one another, pile it all up together, and then cast it into Hell﴾

That is: He gathers it and joins some of it to other parts, until they are piled upon one another because of the extreme crowding, or He adds to the disbeliever what he spent, so that his punishment is increased by the completeness of the hoarders' (kanzin) [guilt].

﴿They﴾ refers to the evil, since it is regarded as the evil group, or to the spenders: ﴿It is they who are the losers﴾, because of their losing themselves and their wealth.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His, the Exalted, Saying:

[38] ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: If they cease, what has passed will be forgiven them; but if they return, then the precedent of the former peoples has already passed.﴾

﴿Say to those who disbelieve﴾: meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions. The definite article here is either for a specific group (al-'ahd) or for the category (al-jins), so these people are included in it at the first level. ﴿If they cease﴾: that is, from disbelief and from fighting the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿What has passed will be forgiven them﴾: that is, of disbelief and sins. ﴿But if they return﴾: to fighting him, ﴿then the precedent of the former peoples has already passed﴾: that is, those who banded together against the prophets and were destroyed, or those whose scheming recoiled upon them on the Day of Badr.

His saying ﴿then the precedent has already passed﴾ and so on is the evidence of the apodosis (jawab), and the implied meaning is: We will take vengeance upon them, for the precedent has already passed......... and so on.

Note:

The verse has been cited as evidence that Islam wipes out what came before it, as has come in the hadith, and that when a disbeliever embraces Islam, he is not required to make up what he missed of prayer, zakat, fasting, or the destruction of property or a life.

The Malikis applied all of that to the apostate who repents, on account of the generality of the verse, and they cited it as evidence for dropping the jizya that was owed by a dhimmi and collected from him before his conversion to Islam.

Ibn Abi Hatim related through the chain of Ibn Wahb from Malik: A disbeliever is not held to account for anything he did in his disbelief once he embraces Islam, and their divorces are not counted as anything, because God, the Exalted, said: ﴿If they cease, what has passed will be forgiven them.﴾ Thus it is in (al-Iklil).

(p-2996) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah. But if they cease, then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾

﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah﴾ i.e., shirk, or misguidance of others, and their fitnah against the believers concerning their religion. ﴿And religion is entirely for Allah﴾ i.e., monotheism becomes sincerely devoted to Allah, so that nothing other than Him is worshipped. ﴿But if they cease﴾ i.e., from disbelief and sins outwardly. ﴿Then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾ i.e., of their inner states, ﴿Seeing﴾ i.e., He will recompense them, and their reckoning rests with Him. So refrain from them, even if you do not know their inner states. Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if they repent, establish the prayer, and give zakah, then let them go on their way﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5], and in the other verse: ﴿then they are your brothers in religion﴾ [al-Tawbah: 11].

In the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, 'There is no god but Allah.' When they say it, they have protected their blood and their property from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

And in the Sahih, "that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Usamah: When that man raised his sword over him and said, 'There is no god but Allah,' and he struck him and killed him, this was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to Usamah: 'Did you kill him after he had said, There is no god but Allah? How will you deal with 'There is no god but Allah' on the Day of Resurrection?' He said: O Messenger of Allah, he only said it out of fear. He said: 'Why did you not split open his heart?' And he kept saying it and repeating it to him: 'Who will be your advocate on the Day of Resurrection with 'There is no god but Allah'?' Usamah said: Until I wished that I had not embraced Islam until that day."

(p-2997)The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[40] ﴿And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your Protector; an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper.﴾

﴿And if they turn away﴾, i.e., they turn away from faith and do not desist. ﴿Then know that Allah is your Protector﴾, i.e., your Helper and Supporter, so trust in His guardianship and His support. ﴿An excellent Protector﴾, so whoever He takes as protector is not lost. ﴿And an excellent Helper﴾, so whoever He helps is not defeated.

Then, exalted is He, explained the destination of what He made lawful for this Ummah and singled it out for them, namely the spoils of war, by His saying, glorified is He:

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[41] ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, one-fifth of it belongs to God, and to the Messenger, and to the near of kin, and the orphans, and the needy, and the wayfarer, if you have believed in God and in what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met. And God is over all things competent.﴾

﴿And know that whatever you obtain of anything﴾, i.e., whether little or much, from the disbelievers. ﴿One-fifth of it belongs to God﴾, i.e., to the One from Whom is the victory, on which the spoils depend. [The fifth is set aside] as thanks to Him for His victory and for granting the spoils. ﴿And to the Messenger﴾, i.e., the one who is the origin of the causes of victory. ﴿And to the near of kin﴾, who are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib. ﴿And the orphans﴾, i.e., those whose fathers have died and who have not reached maturity, because they are weak. ﴿And the needy﴾, because they too are weak, like the orphans. ﴿And the wayfarer﴾, who is the traveler whose road has been cut off and who wishes to return to his land and has nothing with which to reach it.

**On this verse there are several issues:**

**First:** The jurists said: "ghanimah" (spoils of war, the wealth taken from the disbelievers by the pressing of horses and riding animals), i.e., what the Muslims gain through fighting. Is it the same as *fay'* (property gained without fighting) and *nafl* (extra award given by the commander), or not? We will explain this at the end of the issues.

**Second:** The "mā" in ﴿أنَّما﴾ (*annamā*) is in the sense of "that which," and its returning pronoun is omitted. According to their principles, it should have been written separately.

Al-Shihab said: It has also been permitted that this "mā" be conditional.

**Third:** His words ﴿مِن شَيْءٍ﴾ ("of anything") are an explanation of the relative clause. Its position is accusative, being a circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun returning to the relative clause. It is intended to emphasize the importance of the spoils and that nothing should be excluded from them, i.e., whatever you have obtained, of whatever kind, which falls under the name "thing," even a thread or a needle.

**Fourth:** *al-khumus* (the fifth) with a dammah on the *mīm* and with sukūn are two dialects, both of which have been recited.

**Fifth:** The verse indicates that what is obligatory on spoils is that they be divided into five, that the fifth be spent on those whom God Most High mentioned, and that the remainder be divided among the warriors justly: the foot soldier receives one share, and the horseman with an Arabian horse receives three shares, one for himself and two for his horse.

This is how the Prophet (ﷺ) divided [the spoils] in the year of Khaybar.

Among the jurists there are those who say the horseman receives two shares.

The first is what the authentic Sunnah indicates, and because the horse requires its own provision and care, and the benefit of the horseman with it is greater than the benefit of two men.

Among them are those who say that the Arabian horse and the hybrid (*hajīn*) are equal in this. The hybrid is called *al-birdhawn* or *al-akdīsh*.

It is obligatory to divide them among them justly, so that no one is favored, neither for his rank, nor his lineage, nor his merit, as the Prophet (ﷺ) and his successors used to divide them.

In Sahih al-Bukhari: "Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu) thought that he had a superiority over those below him, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Are you helped and provided for except through your weak ones?'" In the Musnad of Ahmad: "Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu) said: 'May your mother be bereaved of you, son of Umm Sa'd!' And are you provided for and helped except through your weak ones?" Thus it is in *al-Siyasa al-Shar'iyya* by Ibn Taymiyya.

In *Zad al-Ma'ad* by Ibn al-Qayyim: "When he (ﷺ) gained victory over his enemy, he would order a caller, who gathered all the spoils, and he began with the spoils (*aslab*), giving them to their owners. Then he set aside one-fifth of the remainder and placed it where God showed him and commanded him, in the interests of Islam. Then he gave a reward (*yarḍakh*) from the remainder to those who had no share, among women, children, and slaves. Then he divided the remainder equally among the army: the horseman three shares, and the foot soldier one share. He would give *nafl* from the core of the spoils according to what he saw as beneficial."

It was also said: Rather, the *nafl* was from the fifth. In some of his campaigns he combined for Salama ibn al-Akwa' the share of the foot soldier and the horseman, giving him five shares, because of the greatness of his service in that expedition.

Ibn Taymiyya said: The spoils continued to be divided among the warriors during the dynasties of the Banu Umayya and the Banu al-‘Abbas, when the Muslims were raiding the Byzantines (al-Rum), the Turks, and the Berbers.

**Sixth:** The majority of scholars held that the mention of God Most High in His words ﴿فَأنَّ لِلَّهِ﴾ ("then to God") is for exalting [the Messenger], i.e., to exalt the Messenger, as in His words: ﴿And God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾ [al-Tawba: 62]. Or it is to show that the fifth must be dedicated to God Most High, and that what is intended is the division of the fifth among those coordinated with it.

Some of them clung to the apparent meaning of this and made obligatory a sixth share for God Most High, to be spent on the ways of good, or to be taken for the Ka'ba. He said: Because the speech of the All-Wise is not devoid of benefit, and because its specification was established in the verse of charity, in His words: ﴿and in the way of God﴾ [al-Tawba: 60], so likewise here.

This is narrated from Abu al-‘Aliya, al-Rabi‘, al-Qasim, and Asbat. What supports the view of the majority is what al-Bayhaqi narrated with an authentic chain from ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from a man who said: "I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was at Wadi al-Qura, and he was leading a horse. I said: 'O Messenger of God! What do you say about the spoils?' He said: 'For God is its fifth, and its four-fifths are for the army.' I said: 'Is there anyone more entitled to it than anyone else?' He said: 'No, not even the arrow you draw from your pocket. You are not more entitled to it than your Muslim brother.'"

Among the subtle points of al-Hasan is that he bequeathed a fifth of his wealth and said: "Shall I not be content with my wealth with what God has been content with for Himself?"

**Seventh:** The Prophet's fifth (ﷺ), which God granted to him, during his lifetime his command over it was entrusted to him, and he disposed of it as he willed and gave it to his community as he wished.

Imam Ahmad narrated that Abu al-Darda' said to ‘Ubada ibn al-Samit: "O ‘Ubada! The words of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the campaign of such-and-such, concerning the fifths?" ‘Ubada said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed with them in their raid, toward a camel from the spoils. When he finished the prayer, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood, took a tuft of hair between his fingertips, and said: 'Indeed this is from your spoils, and there is no share for me in it except my portion with you, except the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you. So return the thread and the needle, and what is larger and smaller than that. Do not commit embezzlement, for embezzlement is a fire and a shame upon its people in this world and the Hereafter. Strive against the people, for the sake of God Blessed and Exalted, the near and the far, and do not fear the blame of any blamer for the sake of God. Establish the limits of God in residence and in travel. Strive in the way of God, for jihad is one of the gates of Paradise, by which God Blessed and Exalted rescues from distress and anxiety.'"

Ibn Kathir said: This is a good and great hadith.

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated from ‘Amr ibn ‘Absa that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed with them toward a camel from the booty. When he finished, he took a tuft of hair from the side of the camel and then said: "It is not lawful for me of your spoils, [even] the like of this, except the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you." It has been used as evidence that he (ﷺ) used to spend it on the interests of the Muslims.

He (ﷺ) had from the spoils something he would select for himself: a slave, or a female slave, or a horse, or a sword, or the like. This was narrated by Abu Dawud from Muhammad ibn Sirin and al-Sha‘bi as a *mursal* report, and by Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi from Ibn ‘Abbas.

Regarding what is done with his fifth (ﷺ) after him, the scholars have several positions:

Some say it goes to the one who holds the leadership after him. Ibn Kathir said: This was narrated from Abu Bakr, ‘Ali, Qatada, and a group. A hadith with a *marfū‘* (traced to the Prophet) chain has also come concerning this.

Some say it is spent on the interests of the Muslims. al-A‘mash narrated from Ibrahim: Abu Bakr and ‘Umar used to allot the Prophet's share (ﷺ) to horses and weapons.

Some say it is spent on his relatives (ﷺ).

Some say it is returned to the remaining categories: the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer. This was chosen by Ibn Jarir. The matter has a basis in reasoning.

**Second:** They agreed that what is meant by "the near of kin" is his relatives (ﷺ).

The majority held that the share of the near of kin is spent exclusively on the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, because the Banu al-Muttalib supported the Banu Hashim in the Jahiliyya and at the beginning of Islam, and they entered with them into the *Shi‘b* (the valley-confinement) out of anger for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and in protection of him: their Muslims out of obedience to God and His Messenger, and their disbelievers out of tribal zeal, pride, and obedience to Abu Talib, the uncle of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

As for the Banu ‘Abd Shams and the Banu Nawfal, although they were the sons of their paternal uncle, they did not agree with them. Rather, they fought them and rejected them, and they colluded with the clans of Quraysh against the Messenger. For this reason Abu Talib censured them in his qasida, saying in it:

*May God repay us against ‘Abd Shams and Nawfal with a punishment of evil, hastened and not delayed.*

(Nawfal: he is the son of Khuwaylid, who was among the devils of Quraysh, and ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib killed him on the day of Badr.)

*By a scale of justice that does not betray a grain, having a witness from itself, not confused.*

(*lā yakhīs*: from the expression *khāsa bi-al-ʿahd*, meaning he broke the covenant and corrupted it. *al-ʿā’il*: the bewildered one.)

*Indeed the wisdom of a people has been foolish, who exchanged for us, in place of us, the Banu Khalaf, and the al-Ghayatil.*

(*qayḍan*: in exchange; *al-Ghayatil*: the Banu Sahm.)

*And we are the purest of the summit of Hashim and the family of Qusayy in the earliest calamities.*

(*al-ṣamīm*: the pure essence of everything; *al-dhu’āba*: the high group, and its origin is a lock of hair from the head.)

Jubayr ibn Mut‘im ibn ‘Adi ibn Nawfal said: "I went, I and ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, to the Prophet (ﷺ), and we said: 'You gave the Banu al-Muttalib from the fifth of Khaybar and left us, while we and they are in one position with respect to you?' He said: 'Indeed the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib are one thing.'" Narrated by Muslim.

In another narration: "They did not separate from me in the Jahiliyya or in Islam." This was cited by Ibn Kathir.

It has been narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, Zayn al-‘Abidin, and al-Baqir that the grant is equalized between their rich and their poor, their males and their females, because the name of kinship includes them, and because they were compensated for it when charity was forbidden to them, and by analogy with property assigned to the sons of such-and-such.

Al-Shafi‘i considered that their share is due by kinship, so it resembles inheritance. He said: So the male receives the equivalent of the share of two females. End of quotation.

In *al-‘Inaya* he said: ‘Abd Manaf, the grandfather of the Prophet (ﷺ), had five sons: Hashim, ‘Abd Shams, Nawfal, al-Muttalib, and Abu ‘Amr, and all of them had offspring except Abu ‘Amr.

**Ninth:** The share of the orphans: it was said it is restricted to their poor, and it was said it includes the rich and the poor, as Ibn Kathir related. The more evident is the second, and the reason for it is what we presented in Surat al-Baqara, so recall it, for it is important.

**Tenth:** The needy (*masakin*): the destitute who do not find what would meet their need and suffice them. As for the wayfarer (*ibn al-sabil*), we mentioned its meaning earlier.

**Eleventh:** Some of them said: What is mentioned in this verse, and what is in the beginning of this surah concerning *al-Anfal*, and what is in Surat al-Hashr in His words ﴿what God has returned as fay' to His Messenger﴾ [al-Hashr: 7], indicates that the division of wealth gained through victory is threefold: *nafl* (extra award), ghanimah (spoils), and fay'. This requires that the granting of the *nafl* be to God and His Messenger, that the ghanimah be for those mentioned, fivefold, and that the fay' be for those mentioned without restriction. The distinction is that each of the three has a ruling that differs from the others: *nafl* is what is given to the one who has, through his exertion and fighting, something others do not have, fulfilling his promise to him in this regard, before the spoils are secured, like the spoils of a slain enemy (*salab*). The ghanimah is what is secured by fighting, apart from what the *nafl* was stipulated for, for it is not subject to the fifth. The fay' is what is taken from the disbelievers without fighting, such as property they make peace over, the *jizya* (poll tax), the *kharaj* (land tax), and the like. The majority held to this detailed distinction.

Some of them went to the unity of the three, the absence of distinction between them, and their inclusion within the ghanimah. He said: What is stated absolutely in the verse of al-Anfal and the verse of al-Hashr is restricted by this verse of ghanimah. This is what is meant by the statement of some that they are *mansukha* (abrogated) by this verse, in the sense that their absolute application is restricted by this one. And God knows best.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿If you have believed in God﴾, i.e., act upon what has been mentioned, and be content with this division, for faith requires acting on knowledge and being content with the ruling.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 41 (part 2 of 2):

It has come in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas, in the hadith of the delegation of Abd al-Qays, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I command you with four things and forbid you from four things: I command you with faith in Allah." (p-3004) Then he said: "Do you know what faith in Allah is? It is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving the zakat, and that you give the fifth of the spoils of war" — the hadith. So he made the payment of the fifth part of the faith. Al-Bukhari also gave it a chapter heading in the Book of Faith in his Sahih, saying: "Chapter: Paying the fifth is part of faith," and he cited the hadith mentioned.

Allah's saying, ﴿And what We sent down﴾, is coordinated with (in Allah), meaning: if you have believed in Allah and in what was sent down ﴿upon Our servant﴾, meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that is, of the signs, the angels, and the victory; ﴿on the day of the Criterion﴾, meaning the day of Badr, for on it He distinguished between truth and falsehood. And "al-Furqan" is in its linguistic meaning, and the idafa (construct) in it is for a known reference. ﴿on the day the two hosts met﴾, meaning the host of the believers and the host of the disbelievers; so the definiteness is for a known reference. Their meeting took place on Friday, the seventeenth day of Ramadan having passed. The believers that day were three hundred and some odd ten men, and the polytheists were between one thousand and nine hundred. So Allah defeated the polytheists, killed from among them more than seventy, and took captive the same number.

﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, so He is able to grant victory to the few over the many, as He did with you on the day of Badr.

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 42:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[42] ﴿When you were on the nearer side of the valley, and they were on the farther side, and the caravan was below you. Had you made an appointment together, you would have differed about the appointment. But it was so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done, that whoever perished might perish by clear proof and whoever lived might live by clear proof. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

﴿Idh antum﴾ is either a substitute (badal) for ﴿the Day of Criterion﴾ [al-Anfal: 41], or an adverbial complement (zarf) of an omitted verb, meaning: remember when you, O assembly of believers, were ﴿on the nearer side of the valley﴾, that is, the edge of the valley nearer to Madinah, ﴿and they﴾, that is (p-3005) the polytheists, Abu Jahl and his companions, ﴿were on the farther side﴾, that is, the more distant from Madinah, on the side nearer Makkah. ﴿And the caravan was below you﴾, that is, the caravan in which Abu Sufyan was, with the merchandise he had, for which the going out had been undertaken, lower than the position of the believers, toward the seashore, three miles from (Badr).

A subtle point:

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, what is the benefit of this specification, and of mentioning the positions of the two groups, and that the caravan was below them? I say: the benefit in it is to inform about the situation that indicates the strength of the enemy's affair, their might, the completeness of their equipment, the preparation of the causes of victory for them, and the weakness of the Muslims' condition and the disorder of their affair. And that their victory in such a situation was nothing but a work from Allah, glorified is He, and a proof that this matter could not have been made easy except by His power and strength and His manifest might. The farther side, where the polytheists alighted, had water and was good land, while the nearer side had no water; it was a soft, loose ground (khabar), which the feet sink into, and one cannot walk on it except with fatigue and hardship. The caravan was behind the backs of the enemy, despite their large number, so the protection of it doubled their zeal and sharpened their intentions in fighting for it. For this reason the Arabs used to go out to war with their women and wealth, so that the defense of the sanctuary and the jealousy for war would drive them to exert their utmost effort in fighting, and so that they would not leave behind them anything they might be tempted to turn toward. That gathers their hearts, controls their anxieties, and settles their souls on not leaving their place, not vacating their positions, and exerting the utmost of their valour and the extreme of their fierceness. In it is also a depiction of what Allah, glorified is He, arranged concerning the event of Badr, so that He might accomplish a matter that was to be done, namely the strengthening of His religion and the elevation of His word, when He promised the Muslims one of the two groups, unspecified and not made clear, until they went out to seize the caravan, desiring to go out, while the Quraysh were moved to panic by what had reached them of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) interference with their wealth, until they set out to protect the others. He arranged the causes until these were settled on the nearer side and those on the farther side, with the caravan behind them, defended by them, until the war stood upon its leg, and what happened happened. End.

Al-Nasir in (al-Intisaf) said: This section is among the excellent distinctions of al-Zamakhshari and his searching out of the secrets of the Noble Book.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had you made an appointment together, you would have differed about the appointment﴾, that is: had you and the people of Makkah agreed on a meeting time at which you would meet for battle, some of you would have opposed others. Your fewness and their fewness would have hindered you from keeping the appointment, and what was in their hearts of awe of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims would have hindered them. Thus the meeting you had would not have come about in the way Allah made it succeed and arranged it. Thus said al-Zamakhshari.

In the hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik, he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims went out only desiring the caravan of Quraysh, until Allah brought them together with their enemy without a prior appointment."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Umayr ibn Ishaq, who said: Abu Sufyan came with the caravan from Syria, and Abu Jahl went out to prevent him from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions. They met at Badr, and neither group knew of the other, nor the other of them, until the water-carriers met and the people saw one another.

﴿But it was so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾, that is: rather, He gathered you in this condition, without a prior appointment, so that He might accomplish what He willed of strengthening Islam and its people and humbling polytheism and its people, without any dispute from you.

As for His saying ﴿that was to be done﴾, that is: fit to be done. It was said: (kana) here means (sara), that is: it became something done, after it had not been. It was said: He expressed it this way to convey its certainty, as if it had already passed.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that whoever perished might perish by clear proof and whoever lived might live by clear proof﴾, that is: He gathered you with your enemy in one place without a prior appointment only so that He might give you victory over them, and raise the proof of truth over falsehood, so that the matter would become manifest, the argument decisive, the proofs shining, and no one would have any argument or doubt left. Then whoever perished would perish, that is, whoever persisted in disbelief would persist in it with insight into his matter, knowing that he is a falsifier, since the proof has been established against him. And whoever believed would believe with certainty and insight and conviction that this is the religion of truth, which must be entered (p-3007) and held fast to.

That is because what occurred at (Badr) was among the bright, radiant signs, such that whoever disbelieves after them is obstinate against himself and deceives himself.

Subtleties:

The first: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that whoever perished might perish﴾ (li-yahlika) is either a substitute for (li-yaqḍiya), or is connected to (maf'ulan).

The second: life and death are a metaphor (isti'ara) for disbelief and faith. It is also read (li-yahlaka) with a fatḥa on the lam.

The third: (ḥayya) is read with a shadda on the yā', which is the original form, since the two letters are identical and both vowelled, so it is like (shadda) and (maddа). From it is the saying of ʿUbayda ibn al-Abras:

"They were perplexed by their affair, as the dove was perplexed by its egg."

It is also read with the two letters separated (idhhār), and there are two explanations for this:

One of them: the past form was modelled on the future form, (yaḥyā). Just as the future is not assimilated, the past is not assimilated either. This is not the case with (shadda) and (madda), for they are assimilated in both forms.

The second explanation: the two letters differ in vowel, the first being kasra and the second fatḥa, and the difference of the two vowels is like the difference of the two letters. For this reason they permitted in the common usage: (laḥaḥtu ʿalayhi) and (ḍabiba al-baladu), when its lizards multiplied. What strengthens this is that the second vowel is incidental, so the second yā' is as if it were quiescent, and if it were quiescent, assimilation would not be required. Likewise when it is in the status of a quiescent letter. The two yā's are original, and the second is not a substitute for a wāw. As for (al-ḥayawān), the wāw in it is a substitution for a yā'. As for (al-ḥiwāʾ), it is not from the word (al-ḥayya), but from (ḥawā yaḥwī) when gathered; thus said Abu al-Baqa'.

﴿And indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾, that is: of the disbelief of the one who disbelieved and its punishment, and of the faith of the one who believed and its reward.

And His saying, exalted is He:

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[43] ﴿When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few. And had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and disputed about the matter, but Allah saved [you]. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾

﴿When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few﴾ is in the accusative case, governed by (remember) [i.e., "remember when..."], or it is another substitution (badal) for (the Day of the Criterion). That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, showed them to him in his vision as few, and he informed his companions of that, and it was a source of reassurance for them and encouragement against their enemy.

﴿And had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage﴾, meaning: you would have been cowardly and shrunk from advancing.

﴿And you would have disputed about the matter﴾, meaning: the matter of advancing and holding back, so your word would have become divided. ﴿But Allah saved [you]﴾, meaning: He protected and graciously granted safety from cowardice and dispute through His support and protection. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, meaning: He knows what will be in them of boldness and cowardice, patience and impatience. Therefore He arranged what He arranged.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[44] ﴿And [remember] when He showed them to you as few in your eyes when you met, and made you appear few in their eyes, that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to Allah are returned [all] matters.﴾

﴿And [remember] when He showed them to you as few in your eyes when you met﴾ This was to confirm the dream of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and so that they would witness directly what he had informed them of, whereby their certainty would increase, they would be earnest, and they would stand firm.

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They were made to appear so few in our eyes that I said to a man beside me: 'Do you think they are seventy?' He said: 'I think they are a hundred!' Then we captured a man from among them and asked him: 'How many were you?' He said: 'A thousand!'" – related by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir.

﴿And He makes you appear few in their eyes﴾ That is, while awake, until Abu Jahl said: "Muhammad and his companions are but a mouthful of camel meat," a proverb for fewness, (like "a mouthful of a head"), meaning that because of their fewness, that amount would suffice them.

"Akalah" (eaters) is in the pattern of "katabah" (scribes), the plural of "akil" (eater), in the pattern of "fa'il". "Al-jazur" is the she-camel. So it is stated in al-'Inayah.

﴿that Allah might accomplish a matter﴾ That is, of manifesting the extraordinary signs that indicate the truth of the religion of Islam and the falsehood of the religion of disbelief.

﴿that was to be done﴾ That is, it was as though its doing were binding upon the All-Wise, because of the great good in it. Said by al-Mahayimi.

(p-3009) Subtleties:

The first: al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: the purpose of making the disbelievers appear few in the eyes of the believers is clear, so what is the purpose of making the believers appear few in the eyes of the disbelievers?"

I say: He made them appear few in their eyes before the encounter, then increased them in their eyes after it, so that they would become bold against them, out of their lack of concern for them; then the multitude would suddenly overtake them, so they would be dumbfounded and fearful, and their strength would be broken, when they see what was not in their reckoning and estimation. This is His saying: ﴿They saw them as twice their number with their own eyes﴾ [Al 'Imran: 13]. And so that they would not prepare against them, and so that the argument against them would be greater through the clarity of the manifest sign, from their fewness at first and their multitude at the end.

The second: al-Zamakhshari also said: "If you ask: by what means do they see the many as few? I say: by Allah concealing part of it from them with a veil, or by creating in their eyes something through which they perceive the many [as few], just as He created in the eyes of the squinting [a condition] by which they see one as two. It was said to one of them: 'The squinter sees one as two,' and there was one rooster before him, so he said: 'Why do I not see these two roosters as four?'" End of quote.

Al-Nasir said in al-Intisaf: "In this – meaning al-Zamakhshari's statement – is clear evidence that Allah the Exalted is the One who creates perception in the sense organ, not contingent upon a cause of facing, nearness, removal of veils, or otherwise. For if these causes were rationally necessitating vision, it would not be possible for Him to conceal part of them from them, while they perceived part, and the necessitating cause is shared.

Accordingly, it is permissible for Allah to create perception together with those causes being present, so there is no necessary connection between seeing and its negation within Allah's power, the Exalted. This refutes the Qadariyyah who deny the vision of Allah the Exalted, on the basis that these causes are considered rationally necessary for the attainment of perception, and that they entail corporeality, since facing, nearness and removal of veils only apply to a body.

So this verse suffices them in refuting their claim, but they pass by it while turning away from it. And Allah is the Granter of success."

The third: It may not be said that His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾ is a repetition of what came before. (p-3010) For we say: the purpose of mentioning it first is their gathering without prior appointment, so that the believers would gain dominance over the polytheists in a manner that constitutes a miracle indicating his truthfulness (ﷺ). The purpose of it here is to explain another extraordinary sign, namely their being made to appear few in the eyes of the polytheists, then their being made to appear many, for the wisdom mentioned earlier.

In His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And to Allah are returned all matters﴾ there is an alert that the states of this world are not intended for their own sake; rather, what is intended from them is what is suitable to be provision for the Day of Return.

Then Allah, exalted is He, guided His believing servants to the etiquettes of encounter on the field of battle and of confronting enemies, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[45] ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company [of the enemy], stand firm and remember Allah much that you may be successful.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company [of the enemy], stand firm⁠﴾ means: when you fight a group, then stand firm for their encounter and be patient in facing them in single combat, so do not flee, do not be cowardly, and do not falter. The interpretation of "encounter" (liqa') as "fighting" (harb) is because it predominates in that sense, as with "nizal" (close combat). He did not describe the company as disbelieving, because that is known and does not need to be stated.

﴿And remember Allah much⁠﴾ means: in the places of battle, seeking support through His remembrance, seeking His help, and invoking Him against your enemy. ﴿that you may be successful⁠﴾ means: that you may attain your aim of victory and reward.

It is established in the two Sahihs from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Awfa that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on one of the days on which he met the enemy, waited until the sun had declined, then stood among the people and said: "O people! Do not wish for the encounter with the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. But when you meet them, be patient, and know that Paradise is under the shade of the swords."

Then he said: "O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Mover of the clouds, Defeater of the confederates, defeat them and grant us victory over them."

The verse also implies that the servant should not slacken in the remembrance of his Lord, most when his heart is most preoccupied and his concern is greatest, and that he should turn to Him in times of hardship, face Him wholeheartedly with a free mind, confident that His kindness never departs from him in any state of affairs. . . .

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[46] ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart; and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾

﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: in everything that they command and forbid. This is general, and singling it out here is for emphasis. ﴿And do not dispute﴾ means: through differing opinions, or concerning what you have been commanded. ﴿Lest you lose courage﴾ means: lest you become cowardly, since some of you would not be strengthened by others.

﴿And your strength depart﴾ means: your power, your dominance, your victory and your state. He likened what was mentioned, in the executing of command and its carrying out, to the wind and its blowing. It is said: "The winds of so-and-so blew," when fortune favoured him and his command was carried out. It has been said:

*When your winds blow, seize them, for every fluttering thing has a stillness.*

*And do not neglect goodness within them, for you do not know when the stillness will come.*

﴿And be patient﴾ means: through the hardships of war, and in opposing your desires that call to dispute. Patience entails victory. ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ means: with victory.

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, in courage and in acting upon what Allah and His Messenger commanded them, and in carrying out what he guided them to, had what no nation or generation before them had, and what no one after them will have. By the blessing of the Messenger (ﷺ) and obedience to him in what he commanded them, they opened hearts and lands from east to west, within a short period and despite their small number relative to the armies of all the regions, (p-3012) of the Romans, Persians, Turks, Slavs, Berbers, Abyssinians, the various kinds of Sudanese, the Copts and the peoples of the children of Adam. They overcame them all, until the word of Allah was exalted and His religion prevailed over all other religions, and the Islamic realms stretched across the eastern and western parts of the earth in less than thirty years. May Allah be pleased with them all and satisfy them.

Note:

Some commentators said, concerning the words of His Exalted saying ﴿and do not dispute﴾: that is, do not differ concerning what He has commanded you regarding jihad; rather, let your opinion be united.

He said: One may say that from this is derived the obligation to appoint a commander over the army to direct its affairs and to end their disagreement, for by the obligation to obey him, disagreement ends. The Prophet (ﷺ) did this in the expeditions, and he said: "Listen and obey, even if a black Abyssinian slave is appointed over you." End of quotation.

When Exalted Allah commanded the believers to steadfastness and patience at the encounter, He commanded them to sincerity in it, by forbidding them from imitating the polytheists in their setting out for show, saying, glorified is He:

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:**

[47] ﴿And do not be like those who left their homes insolent and to be seen by people, and who bar from the way of Allah. And Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾

﴿And do not be like those who left their homes **insolently** (*bataran*)﴾, meaning: boasting of bravery. ﴿And to be seen by people (*ri'a' al-nas*)﴾, meaning: seeking praise for generosity and courage. ﴿And who bar from the way of Allah. And Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾ That is, do not be like Abu Jahl and his companions.
