When Abu Sufyan's messenger came to them while they were at al-Juhfa, telling them to turn back because their caravan was safe, they refused and said: "We will not turn back until we reach Badr, where we will slaughter camels, serve wine, and have singing girls play for us, so that the Arabs will hear of us." That was their insolence and their showing off to people through feeding them. So they came to it, and they were given the cups of death in place of wine, and the wailing women mourned over them in place of the singing girls. The meaning is: let your affair not be for show, nor for reputation, nor for seeking what is in the sight of people. Purify your intention and your seeking of reward for Allah in supporting your religion and aiding your Prophet. Do not act except for that, and do not seek anything else.

The word **riya'** (showing off) is the verbal noun of *raa'a*, when one displays an act to people so that they will see it, out of heedlessness of the Creator. It is also said *raayaahu muraayaatan wa riyaa'an*, with metathesis (*'alā al-qalb*).

In ﴿*bataran wa ri'a'*﴾, they may be an object of purpose (*maf'ūl min ajlihi*), or a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*).

**Yaṣuddūna** may be a circumstantial clause, by interpreting it as an active participle, or by taking it as the verbal noun of a verb that is itself a circumstantial clause; or it may be a new, independent clause (*musta'naf*).

The subtlety of expressing the first items by nouns and then by a verb is to inform that insolence and showing off are their habitual conduct, unlike barring from the way, which renewed for them in the time of prophethood.

The statement concerning His words, exalted is He:

[48] ﴿When Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them and said, "No one among the people will overcome you today, and I am a protector for you." But when the two hosts came into view, he turned back on his heels and said, "I am free of you. I see what you do not see. I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment."﴾.

﴿When Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them﴾, i.e., in opposing the Messenger and the believers, by whispering to them. ﴿And said, "No one among the people will overcome you today"﴾, i.e., from the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. ﴿"And I am a protector for you"﴾, i.e., a granter of protection and a helper for you. ﴿But when the two hosts came into view﴾, i.e., when they met, and each host saw the other, and he saw the angels descending from the sky to support the believers. ﴿He turned back on his heels﴾, i.e., he fled, turning his back. ﴿And said, "I am free of you"﴾, i.e., from the covenant of your protection. ﴿"I see what you do not see"﴾, i.e., the angels descending to support the believers. ﴿"I fear Allah"﴾, i.e., that He may punish me before the Day of Resurrection. ﴿"And Allah is severe in punishment"﴾, i.e., it is not unlikely, given that He has granted me respite until the Resurrection, that He will punish me because of the severity of His punishment.

Note:

They mentioned two views concerning the "making seem attractive":

The first: that Satan whispered to them without any form of embodiment, not in the shape of a man. This is related from al-Hasan and al-Asamm.

According to this view, "said" is a metaphor for whispering, and "turned back" (nukus, meaning retreat) is a metaphor for the nullification of his scheme.

The second: that he appeared in the form of a man. When they wanted to set out for Badr, they feared the Banu Kinanah, because they had killed a man and the Banu Kinanah were seeking his blood. They were not secure against being attacked from behind, so Iblis the accursed took the form of Suraqah al-Kinani and said, "I am your protector against the Banu Kinanah; no harm from them will reach you." Thus his saying "I am a protector for you" is literal.

The Imam said: The meaning of "protector" (jar) here is one who repels harm from his companion, just as a neighbour repels harm from his neighbour. The Arabs say, "I am your protector against so-and-so," meaning: I am guarding you and preventing him from you. This second view is the view of the majority of the exegetes.

Malik related in the Muwatta' (a collection of hadith compiled by Malik ibn Anas), from Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Kurayz, as a mursal report, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Satan was never seen on any day smaller, more humiliated, more despised, or more enraged than on the Day of 'Arafah.»

That is only because of what he sees of the descent of mercy and Allah's forgiveness of great sins. The exception is what he saw on the Day of Badr, for he saw Jibril marshalling the angels.

The Imam said: The change of Iblis's form into the form of Suraqah was a great miracle for the Messenger ﷺ. This is because when the Quraysh disbelievers returned to Makkah, they said, "The people have defeated Suraqah." News of this reached Suraqah, and he said, "By Allah, I was not aware of your departure until your defeat reached me." At that point it became clear to the people that the person in question had not been Suraqah, but rather a devil.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[49] ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "These people have been deluded by their religion." But whoever relies upon Allah — indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾

﴿When the hypocrites say﴾, i.e., in Medina. The word ﴿when﴾ (idh) is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb "remember" (udhkur), or by "adorned" (zayyana) [in verse 48].

﴿And those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ may be a description of the hypocrites, and the conjunction "and" (wa) is placed in between to emphasize the close attachment of the description to the one described, since this is a description of the hypocrites that never leaves them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿in whose hearts is a disease﴾. Or the "and" may be inserted between the explained and the explanation, as in the expression: "Zayd impressed me, and his generosity" (a'jabanī Zaydun wa karamuhu).

It may also be intended: "those who are on the edge," who are not firm of foot in Islam.

It is reported from al-Hasan that they are the polytheists.

﴿Has deluded these people﴾, meaning the believers, ﴿their religion﴾, so they thought that they would be supported by it over their multitudes. ﴿But whoever relies upon Allah — indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise﴾, i.e., whoever depends upon Him, glorified and exalted is He, He will grant him victory over his multitudes, however numerous they may be, because He is Exalted in Might, Overpowering in what He wills, and He wills the victory of His allies, and He is Wise, and His wisdom requires their victory. This is an answer to them from Him, exalted is He, and a rejection of their statement.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying:

[50] ﴿And if you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs, [saying], "Taste the punishment of the Burning."﴾

﴿And if you could see when those who disbelieve are taken﴾, i.e., the angels take their souls, (the angels), i.e., the angels of subjugation and punishment, in a manner suited to the states of their souls. ﴿striking their faces﴾ because of their turning away from the truth, and because of the states of arrogance, self-admiration and haughtiness within them; ﴿and their backs﴾ because of their inclination toward falsehood, their intense attraction to it, and the states of desire, greed and voracity. ﴿"Taste the punishment of the Burning."﴾ is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with (striking), with the saying elided (idmār al-qawl), i.e., they say, "Taste," as good tidings to them of the punishment of the Hereafter. The response of (if, law) is omitted, to magnify and dramatize the matter.

Ibn Kathir said: This context, although its occasion was the Battle of Badr, is general in regard to every disbeliever. In Surat Muhammad there is a verse like this one, and earlier in al-Anʿam there is something similar, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death and the angels are extending their hands [saying], "Bring out your souls"﴾ [al-Anʿam: 93], i.e., striking them, by the command of their Lord.

(p-3016) The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[51] ﴿That is because of what your hands have sent forth, and because Allah is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾

﴿That﴾ refers to what was mentioned of striking and punishment. ﴿Because of what your hands have sent forth﴾ means: because of what you have earned of disbelief and disobedience. ﴿And because Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ means: that He would seize them without a crime.

If it is asked: what is the secret in using the intensive form ظَلَّامٍ (ẓallām, "one who is greatly unjust"), when negating the essence of injustice is more emphatic than negating its abundance, and negating abundance does not negate its root but may even suggest its existence, and the negation returns to the qualifier?

It is answered with several responses:

Among them: it is a negation of the root of injustice and of its abundance, considering the individual instances of those who do wrong. It is as if it were said: he wrongs so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so on. When these were gathered, the form ظَلَّامٍ (ẓallām) was used for that reason, that is, for the abundance of quantity in it.

Among them: when abundant injustice is negated, minor injustice is negated too, because one who does wrong does so for the benefit gained from wrongdoing. When its abundance is abandoned, despite its greater benefit with respect to one who may benefit or be harmed, then for its little amount, with its little benefit, abandonment is greater.

Among them: ظَلَّامًا (ẓallāman) is for attribution, like مَطَّارٍ (maṭṭār, "one who is attributed with much rain" or "one attributed with frequent travel"); that is, injustice is not attributed to Him at all.

Among them: every attribute of His, Exalted is He, is at the most perfect level. So if He, Exalted is He, were unjust, He would be ẓallām, so the necessary consequence is negated in order to negate what necessitates it.

Among them: in ظَلَّامٍ (ẓallām) there is a negation of the one who does wrong, since it is necessary that when injustice is negated, its perfection is negated too. So the negation of the intensive is made a kināyah (an allusive expression) for the negation of its root, moving from the necessary consequence to what it necessitates.

Among them: punishment is so great that, were it not for deserving, the one punished with its like would be a ẓallām, one of extreme and grave injustice. So the purpose is to declare Him free of it, Exalted is He, and this is worthy of intensification.

Also: if Exalted is He were to punish His servants without deserving and without cause, that would be a great injustice, because it would proceed from the Just and Merciful. Thus [it is stated] in al-ʿInāyah (a commentary on al-Bayḍāwī's work).

(p-3017) In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Exalted is He, says: 'O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, these are only your deeds which I record for you; so whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame none but himself.'" The hadith is lengthy and sublime, and it is known among the scholars of hadith as al-Musalsal bi'l-Dimashqiyyin (a hadith transmitted in a chain of linked transmitters, here named after the people of Damascus).

Then Exalted is He explained that the continuous course of the polytheists and their constant custom, despite what the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent with, is like the course of the earlier nations with their messengers, by His saying, Exalted is He:

The discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[52] ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, who denied the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is Strong and severe in punishment.﴾

﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: the practice of these people is like the practice of the people of Pharaoh and of those among the nations who preceded them, such as the people of Noah. It is their deed, which they persisted in (da'abu, i.e., they continued upon it). Then He explained it, saying: ﴿they denied the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them﴾, i.e., before the Day of Resurrection. ﴿for their sins﴾, i.e., just as He seized these ones, because they became bold in disobeying Him, relying on the strength they saw in themselves, so He humbled them, showing His strength.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong and severe in punishment﴾. Al-Mahayimi said: The delay of punishment is only out of mercy, but when their obstinacy intensified, His anger intensified, for He is severe in punishment toward whoever persists in opposing Him, so there is no mercy in regard to such a person.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[53] ﴿That is because Allah never changes a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves. And indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

﴿That﴾, i.e., the punishment, whose being a seizing to account for sins is known. ﴿Because Allah﴾, i.e., on account of the fact that He, Exalted is He, ﴿never changes a blessing He has bestowed upon a people﴾ by replacing it with a vengeance.

﴿Until they change what is in themselves﴾ of the obligations of those blessings, of belief, or of speech, or of knowledge.

This is an informing about the completeness of His justice and equity in His judgment, that He, Exalted is He, does not change a blessing He has bestowed upon anyone except because of a sin that he committed, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11].

Al-Qashani said: Everything that reaches a person is what his readiness (isti'dad) requires, and he asks for it through the supplication of his state and the request of entitlement.

So when He bestows upon someone a blessing, outward or inward, because his readiness is sound and the goodness in him remains, He does not change it until he corrupts his readiness and alters his receptivity to righteousness, through veiling and the transformation of the goodness within him into evil in potential, owing to the accumulation of rust and the piling up of darkness in him, to the point that he has no further affinity for goodness and no possibility of its issuing from him. Then He changes it into vengeance, as a justice from Him and a grace, and as a demand from that readiness for it through the attraction of kinship and affinity, not as oppression or injustice. End of quote.

﴿And indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾, i.e., so He changes when they change, out of anger toward them, by what He hears from them or knows of them.

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 54:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[54] ﴿As was the case with the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins and drowned the people of Pharaoh, and all of them were wrongdoers.﴾

﴿As was the case with the people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾: the beginning of their change was that they ﴿denied the signs of their Lord﴾, i.e., the One who nurtured them with blessings, and they diverted those blessings to other than the purpose for which they were created, contrary to what those signs required, and so these became sins. ﴿So We destroyed them﴾, i.e., in addition to depriving them of blessings, ﴿for their sins﴾, i.e., because of what they diverted the blessings to other than their created purpose. ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾ because of their drowning the blessings in the sea of denial, by attributing them to Pharaoh, since they acknowledged his divinity. ﴿And all﴾, i.e., of the disbelieving denying groups, or of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, and the disbelievers of Quraysh.

﴿They were wrongdoers﴾, i.e., by diverting the blessings to other than their created purpose, which is a kind of drowning of them in the sea of denial, because it is the source of their change. Thus did al-Mahayimi interpret it.

In this there is an indication of dismissing the apparent repetition in the two verses, through the change of the two comparisons within them, so there is no need to claim emphasis. The meaning of the first: the condition of these people is like the condition of the people of Pharaoh in disbelief, so He seized them and brought upon them punishment. The meaning of the second: the condition of these people is like the condition of the people of Pharaoh in changing their blessings, and God's changing of their condition as a consequence of that change, namely that He drowned them.

It has been said: the composition rejects this, because the point of comparison in the first is their disbelief, which entails punishment, so its point in the second should be His saying "they denied," since it is similar to it, as each of them is an independent clause following a comparison, suitable to be the point of resemblance; so it is to be understood accordingly, like His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59]. As for His saying: ﴿That is because God would never change a blessing He had bestowed﴾ [al-Anfal: 53], it is like the causal explanation for the descent of the retribution, interposed between the two comparisons, not specific to one people; so making it the point of comparison is far from eloquence. Thus in al-'Inayah.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[55] ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, so they will not believe.﴾

﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve﴾ – i.e., they persisted in their disbelief and became firmly rooted in it. ﴿So they will not believe﴾ – i.e., no belief is to be expected from them.

(p-3020) The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[56] ﴿Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear (Allah).﴾

﴿Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear (Allah).﴾ That is: they do not fear the consequence of treachery, nor do they care about the shame and the Fire that it entails.

Admonitions:

First: Al-Mahayimi said: He, Exalted is He, indicates how He would abandon His blessings upon one who changes the states that were the causes of the blessings, and through which he had his humanity. So by changing them he has joined the beasts, and by denying the Benefactor he has become worse than them. Blessings are taken away from one who does not know their worth, so how could they not be taken away from one who denies the Benefactor?

Second: The verse indicates the permissibility of belittling and disparaging the disobedient, in that God, Exalted is He, called them "beasts" (dawabb) and informed that they are "the worst of beasts" (sharr al-dawabb).

Third: They said: The verse was revealed concerning the Jews of Banu Qurayza, the company of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made a covenant with them that they would not fight him nor assist anyone against him. They broke the covenant and aided the polytheists of Makkah with weapons in fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. Then they said: "We forgot and erred," so he made a covenant with them a second time, and they broke the covenant again. They also colluded with the disbelievers against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq). Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf rode to Makkah and agreed with them to oppose the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Fourth: (alladhina) is a substitute (badal) for the first relative pronoun, or an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan) to it, or in the accusative as an expression of censure (nasb ʿala al-dhamm). The verb ﴿ʿaahadta﴾ carries the sense of "taking," which is why it takes (min), meaning: you took from them their covenant.

It has also been said that (min) is superfluous (silah). Abu Hayyan said: it is for partitive meaning (li al-tab'idh), because those who directly undertake the covenant are only some of the people, namely the leaders and the nobles.

Fifth: His saying ﴿and they do not fear (Allah)﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of ﴿yanqudun﴾, meaning: they persist in breaking (the covenant), while the state is that they do not fear the shame in it. This is because the custom of one who has religion, intellect and resolve is to avoid breaking a covenant, so that people feel at ease with his word and trust his speech. Thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes clear that whoever combines disbelief with breaking the covenant is worse than the beasts.

Then He, Exalted is He, began to explain the rulings concerning those who break covenants, after detailing their conditions, with His saying:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[57] ﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war, then drive away with them those behind them, that they may remember.﴾

﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war﴾ means: if you encounter them and prevail over them. ﴿Then drive away with them those behind them﴾ means: scatter by means of them those behind them of the fighters, that is, do to them such punishment and severe chastisement as will drive others away out of fear, so that they become a lesson for them. As He said: ﴿that they may remember﴾, meaning: perhaps those who are driven away will take warning from what they witnessed of what befell those who broke the covenant, so that they refrain from breaking it or from disbelief.

In (al-Taj) it is said: It has also been said that the meaning of ﴿fa-sharrid bihim﴾ is "then make others hear of them" (fa-sammi' bihim), and it has been said: "then frighten by them" (fa-zzi' bihim). It is not hidden that these meanings are close to one another.

The root of al-tashrid is driving away and scattering. It is said: "sharrada bihi tashridan," meaning he made people hear of his faults. He said:

I roam the valleys every day, fearing that Hakim will make others hear of me [and so drive me away].

Its meaning is that he will make others hear of me. Hakim is a man from Bani Sulaym whom the Quraysh had entrusted with restraining the hands of the foolish.

It was cited in (Lisan al-Arab) under the root: sh-r-d.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 58:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[58] ﴿And if you fear from a people treachery, then throw back to them [their treaty] on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not like the treacherous.﴾

﴿And if you fear from a people treachery﴾ is an explanation of the rulings concerning those who are about to break the covenant, following the explanation of those who have already broken it in practice. Here "fear" (al-khawf) is used metaphorically for knowledge, meaning: and if you come to know from a people among the covenanted ones that they will break the covenant in the future, through the signs of treachery and the indications of evil that have become apparent to you from them.

﴿Then throw back to them﴾ meaning: then cast their covenant back to them, ﴿on equal terms﴾ meaning: on a level path, with the intention that you make the breaking known to them and inform them openly that you have cut off what was between you and them of connection, and do not engage them in war while they still assume the covenant remains, so that there is not on your part any trace of treachery at all, even if it is in response to their treachery.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not like the treacherous﴾, is the reason given for the command to throw back [the treaty]. It may be in view of its implying the prohibition of launching battle unannounced, since that would be treachery; so it is a warning to him, peace be upon him, against it. Or it may be in view of its entailing fighting, so it is an exhortation to him, peace be upon him, first to throw back [the treaty], and second to fight them, as if it were said: "And if you know from a people treachery, then throw back to them, then fight them, for Allah does not like the treacherous, and they are among them, and because of what you know of their condition." This is what Abu al-Su'ud conveyed.

Note:

The verse indicates the permissibility of concluding a covenant with disbelievers for a benefit, and the obligation to fulfil the covenant when no sign of treachery appears from them. It also indicates the permissibility of renouncing the covenant for one who anticipates from them the danger of deceit, and that he should inform them of that, lest they blame us for waging war while a covenant is in force.

The compilers of the Sunan related that there was a covenant between Mu'awiyah and the Romans, and he was marching towards their lands so that he would be close, until the covenant expired and he would raid them. A man came upon a horse or a mule, saying: "Allah is greatest! Allah is greatest! Fulfilment, not treachery!" It was 'Amr ibn 'Abasah, and Mu'awiyah sent for him and asked him, and he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever has between himself and a people a covenant, let him not tighten a knot nor loosen it until its term expires, or throw back to them on equal terms.'" So Mu'awiyah turned back.

Imam Ahmad related from Salman al-Farisi that he came to a fortress or a city, and said to his companions: "Leave me to call them as I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) call them." He said:

"I was only a man from among you, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, guided me to Islam. If you embrace Islam, then you will have what we have, and you will have what we have upon you. If you refuse, then pay the jizyah while you are humbled. If you refuse, we will throw back to you on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not like the treacherous."

He did this to them for three days, and when the fourth day came, the people went out to it and conquered it.

This, moreover, concerns the one whose informing them is obligatory, and that is only when there is fear of treachery from them and anticipation of it, as is the literal meaning of the verse.

As for when the breaking of the covenant becomes apparent with certainty, then there is no need for the imam to renounce the covenant; rather he acts as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did with the people of Makkah when they broke the covenant by killing Khuza'ah, while the latter were under the protection of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They were not alarmed except by the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Marr al-Zahran, which was four farsakh from Makkah.

(p. 3024) The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[59] ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think that they have escaped; indeed, they cannot cause [Allah] to fail.﴾

﴿Let not [them] think﴾ is read with the ya' and with the ta'. ﴿Those who disbelieved have escaped﴾ means they got away and slipped free ﴿from being overtaken by Him﴾. ﴿Indeed, they cannot cause [Allah] to fail﴾ means they cannot escape Allah from retribution, either in this world by killing, or in the Hereafter by the punishment of the Fire.

It is also read with the fath of (inna) according to an estimate of the lam al-ta'lil (the lam of causation, "because"). This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us? Evil is what they judge﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 4], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape [Allah] in the earth; their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾ [al-Nur: 57], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the land deceive you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 196] ﴿[It is] a brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Al 'Imran: 197].

And His saying, exalted is He:

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 8, verse 60:

On the interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying:

[60] ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war, by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know, [but] Allah knows them. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.﴾

﴿And prepare against them﴾ meaning: for fighting those who break the covenant mentioned previously, or the disbelievers in general, and the latter is more suited to the context of the noble arrangement. ﴿Whatever you are able of power﴾ meaning: of everything by which one strengthens oneself in war, of its equipment. He called it "power" as an intensification.

Al-Shihab said: It was mentioned because at (Badr) they did not have complete preparation, so they were alerted to the fact that victory without preparation is not attainable in every age.

﴿And of steeds of war﴾ (al-ribat) is originally the verbal noun of rabata, meaning he tied or bound fast, and it is used in the sense of the thing tied in general; its use became frequent for the horses that are tied in the cause of Allah. The idafa (annexation) is either in consideration of the general scope of the original meaning, or in view of the fact that ribat is shared among other meanings, such as waiting for prayer, remaining on the frontier of the enemy, and persevering in a matter; so its annexation to one of its meanings is for clarification, like "the eye of the sun." From this it is known that it is permissible to annex a thing to itself when it is shared.

And if it is from the annexation of the general to the specific, then it is in the sense of the partitive (min).

Ribat may also be the plural of rabit, like fasil and fisal.

In al-Taj it is said: "How excellent is this rabit," referring to what is tied of horses. Then, its being conjoined to "power," although it is part of it, serves to announce its superiority over the rest of its kind, like the conjunction of Gabriel and Michael with the angels.

﴿By which you terrify﴾ meaning: you frighten, by that preparation, ﴿the enemy of Allah﴾, who is the one who ascribes a partner to Him and nullifies His word, ﴿and your enemy﴾ meaning: the one who displays his enmity towards you, so you frighten them lest they fight you, believing in the power they possess themselves, apart from you.

Note:

This verse indicates the obligation of preparing military strength, to guard against the enemy's might and attack.

When the rulers acted in accordance with the requirement of this verse, in the days of the flourishing of Islam, Islam was mighty and great, unyielding to oppression, strong of spear, majestic in standing, abundant in radiance, when the banner of its authority was unfurled over the expanse of the earth, seizing the forelock of the regions and the cities, breaking the thorn of the arrogant disbelievers, pushing back the veils of oppression and enslavement, and its sons lived for successive ages while they were masters of nations, leaders of peoples, the reins of power and strength, and the pole of the two poles of honour and glory, not yielding to strength nor fearing any assault.

As for today, the Muslims have abandoned working by this noble verse, and inclined to luxury and comfort, so they neglected an obligation of the communal duties (fard kifaya), and the whole Ummah has become sinful by abandoning this duty; therefore it suffers today from its distress as it suffers. And how would the enemy not covet the Islamic lands, when you see in them no factories for weapons and war munitions, but rather all of them are bought from the lands of the enemy?

Has not the time come for it to awaken from its heedlessness, and establish factories for manufacturing cannons, rifles, shells and military munitions? For the enemy's diminishing of its lands from their edges has cast upon it a lesson it must reflect upon, and make up for what it neglected before what remains of it is overtaken by his horse and foot, so that he decides - and Allah forbid - upon Islam and the lands of the Muslims, for the colonisation of the cities, the enslavement of the free, and the removal of independence which heralds ruin. And with Allah is guidance.

His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And others﴾ meaning: and you will terrify other people ﴿besides them﴾ meaning: besides those who display their enmity toward you, and they are the hypocrites ﴿whom you do not know﴾ meaning: that they are hostile to you ﴿Allah knows them﴾ meaning: that they are your enemies, who display their enmity when they see your weakness.

Then He, glorified is He, encouraged them to spend wealth on preparing power and tying horses, giving them good news that its reward would be repaid in full, by His saying: ﴿And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah﴾ meaning: which the jihad makes clear, ﴿will be fully repaid to you﴾ meaning: in this world, from the fay', the booty, the jizya and the kharaj, and in the Hereafter with lasting reward; ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾ meaning: by withholding the recompense.

Remarks:

First: This verse is the basis for everything that must be prepared for jihad of equipment.

Second: In His saying ﴿by which you terrify﴾ there is an indication of avoiding that the preparation be for other than terrifying, such as vanity.

In the hadith of Imam Malik from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Horses are of three kinds: for a man it is a reward, for a man it is a shield, and for a man it is a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward, it is a man who tied it in the cause of Allah, and a man who tied it for self-sufficiency and chastity, and did not forget the right of Allah in its necks or its backs; so it is a shield for him. And a man who tied it out of pride, showing off, and enmity toward the people of Islam, so it is a burden upon him in that case."

Third: What we have mentioned in the interpretation of "others," that they are the hypocrites, is witnessed by His, may He be exalted, saying:

﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become obstinate in hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 101]

Then He, may He be exalted, clarified the permissibility of making peace with the disbelievers by His saying:

(p-3027)The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[61] ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it too, and put your trust in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

﴿And if they incline﴾, i.e., they lean toward and submit to ﴿peace﴾ — with a kasra or a fatha on the sin (sin being pronounced both ways, two dialectal forms, and both have been recited) — meaning reconciliation and submission, with fear falling into their hearts upon witnessing the preparedness that you have and the equipment you have amassed. ﴿Then incline to it too﴾, i.e., then tend toward agreeing with them, make peace with them and covenant with them, even if you are able to fight them, because agreement is more conducive to their embracing faith.

For this reason, when the polytheists requested a truce at al-Hudaybiyah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, and the laying down of war between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for ten years, he agreed to that, along with the other conditions they stipulated. And (al-salm, "peace") is both masculine and feminine, as stated in the _al-Qamus_.

Al-Zamakhshari said: (al-salm) is treated as feminine in the manner of its opposite, which is war (al-harb).

Al-Abbas ibn Mirdas said:

"Peace: take from it what pleases you,
and war will suffice you, with only sips of its breaths."

﴿And put your trust in Allah﴾, i.e., do not fear their deceit in the reconciliation, for He will protect you from their deceit. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾ of their sayings ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, i.e., of their conditions, so He will hold them accountable for what they deserve and will turn their scheming back against their own necks.

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*, explanation of the meaning) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[62] ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is Allah. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers.﴾

﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾ means: by [offering] peace, so that you refrain from them outwardly, while in their intention is treachery. ﴿Then sufficient for you is Allah﴾ means: He suffices you with His victory and His aid.

Mujahid said: He means Quraydhah.

Then He gave the reason for His sufficiency for him by what He bestowed upon him of supporting him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with His help and with the believers. So He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿It is He who supported you with His help﴾ means: on the day of Badr, after weakness, without preparing strength or stationing troops at the frontier (*ribat*): ﴿and with the believers﴾

(p-3028) Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[63] ﴿And He joined their hearts together. Had you spent all that is on the earth, you could not have joined their hearts together, but Allah joined them together. Indeed, He is Exalted in Might, Wise.﴾

﴿And He joined their hearts together﴾ meaning: He brought together their hearts and their word, through the guidance with which Allah sent you to them, after there had been in them tribal partisanship (ʿaṣabiyya) and rancour (ḍaghīna). ﴿Had you spent all that is on the earth﴾ meaning: of gold and silver, ﴿you could not have joined their hearts together﴾, since that does not fall within the capacity of humans, because it belongs to the unseen realm. ﴿But Allah joined them together﴾ meaning: joined their hearts together through His religion, to which He gathered them. ﴿Indeed, He is Exalted in Might﴾ meaning: dominant in His kingdom and authority over every outward and inward thing. ﴿Wise﴾ meaning: His wisdom required that, because of what it contains of strengthening His religion and elevating His word.

Al-Zamakhshari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The joining together of the hearts of those to whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent is among the dazzling signs, for the Arabs, because of the zeal (ḥamiyya), tribal partisanship, and concealing of rancour that were in them over the slightest matter, and the throwing of it before their eyes, and their desire to take revenge, two of them hardly could be brought together. Then their hearts were united upon following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they became unified and began shooting from one bow. That was because of what Allah arranged of their harmony, and gathered of their word, and created among them of mutual love and affection, and removed from them of hatred and mutual loathing, and imposed upon them love for the sake of Allah and hatred for the sake of Allah. None can do that except One who controls the hearts; He turns them as He wills and does in them what He intends.

It was also said: they are the Aws and the Khazraj. Between them were wars and battles that destroyed their masters and chiefs and crushed their skulls, and their enmities had no limit or end, and between them was proximity which stirs up grudges and perpetuates envy and rivalry.

The custom of any two groups in such a状态 is that each avoids what the other prefers, dislikes it and recoils from it. So Allah the Exalted made them forget all of that, until they agreed upon obedience, became sincere toward one another, became helpers and then aides.

Nothing of this was except by His subtle creation and perfect power. End of quotation.

(p-3029) The second opinion was weakened only because there is no contextual indicator for it in the context. Thus in al-ʿInaya.

I say: yet the notoriety of the enmity that existed between these two tribes, which had lasted a long time, and whose water had become impossible to drain before the mission, may serve as an indicator. The scholars of the biography (sīra) reported that when the Prophet ﷺ met a group of the Khazraj at the season (of pilgrimage) and invited them to Allah the Exalted, they responded to him and believed him, and said to him: "We have left our people, and there is no people among whom there is as much enmity and evil as among them, and perhaps Allah will unite them through you. We will go to them and call them to your affair, presenting to them what we have accepted from this religion; if Allah unites them upon it, there will be no man mightier than you." Narrated by Ibn Ishaq and others.

And in the two Sahihs: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed the Ansar concerning the spoils of Hunayn, he said to them: 'O assembly of the Ansar! Did I not find you misguided and Allah guided you through me? And poor and Allah enriched you through me? And you were divided and Allah united you through me?' Whenever he said something, they said: 'Allah and His Messenger are more gracious.'"

A subtle point:

Al-Hakim narrated that Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: "Indeed the ties of kinship may be severed, and blessings may be denied, but when Allah brings hearts close together, nothing can move them." Then he recited: ﴿Had you spent all that is on the earth﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Bayhaqi has something similar. And a poet said:

"If a near relative cuts you off with a lapse, and deceives you and becomes self-sufficient, he is no kinsman.
But the near relative who, if you call him, responds, and would strike the enemy you strike..."

(p-3030) He said: Among that is the saying of another:

"I have associated with people, then tested them, and tried what means they reached.
Then kinship does not bring near one who severs, and affection is the nearest of means."

Al-Bayhaqi said: I do not know whether this is connected to the words of Ibn ʿAbbas, or is the saying of one of the narrators after him.

Al-Razi said: Our companions argued from this verse that the states of hearts, of beliefs and volitions, are all created by Allah the Exalted, because the union, affection and intense love came about through faith and following the Messenger ﷺ. End of quotation.

When He, the Exalted, had explained His sufficiency for His Prophet ﷺ against the deception of enemies in the preceding verse, He informed him of His sufficiency for him in all his affairs absolutely, so He said, exalted is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[64] ﴿O Prophet, sufficient for you is Allah and whoever follows you of the believers.﴾

﴿O Prophet, sufficient for you is Allah and whoever follows you of the believers.﴾ The scholar Ibn al-Qayyim said in the introduction to (Zad al-Ma'ad), in explaining this verse: That is, Allah alone is sufficient for you and sufficient for your followers, so they need no one besides Him.

Then he said: Here there are two possible analyses.

The first: the waw is conjunctive, joining (man, "whoever") to the kaf in (kafika, "you") which is in the genitive. Conjoining to a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition is permissible according to the preferred school, and its evidence is abundant, and the arguments against it are feeble.

The second: the waw is the waw of (ma'a, "together with"), and (man) is in the accusative position, in coordination with the place (mahall) of the phrase, for (hasbuka) carries the meaning of (kafika, "sufficient for you"), i.e., Allah suffices you and suffices whoever follows you, just as the Arabs say: "Sufficient for you and Zayd is a dirham." The poet said:

"When the battle rages and the staffs are split, sufficient for you and al-Dahhak is a sword well-tempered."

And this is the more correct of the two analyses. There is also a third analysis: that (man) is in the nominative position as the subject of an inceptive sentence, (p-3031) meaning: "and whoever follows you of the believers, Allah is sufficient for them."

There is also a fourth analysis, which is erroneous in meaning: that (man) is in the nominative position in coordination with the name of Allah, the meaning being: "Sufficient for you is Allah and your followers."

This, though some people have said it, is pure error, and it is not permissible to read the verse as such, for sufficiency and adequacy belong to Allah alone, as do reliance, piety and worship.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then indeed sufficient for you is Allah; it is He who supported you with His help and with the believers.﴾ [al-Anfal: 62] Thus He distinguished between sufficiency and support: He made sufficiency for Him alone, and made support by His help and by His servants. Allah the Glorified praised the people of tawhid and reliance among His servants, in that they devoted sufficiency to Him alone, saying: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it increased them in faith and they said, "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 173]

They did not say, "Sufficient for us is Allah and His Messenger." If this is what they said, and the Lord the Exalted praised them for it, how then would He say to His Messenger: "Allah and your followers are sufficient for you"? And his followers have singled out the Lord the Exalted for sufficiency and did not associate His Messenger with Him. This is among the most impossible of impossibilities and the most false of falsehoods. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿And if they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, "Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and His Messenger, indeed we are turning to Allah,"﴾ [al-Tawbah: 59] So consider how He attributed the giving to Allah and to His Messenger, as He said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾ [al-Hashr: 7], and He made sufficiency for Him alone. He did not say, "and they said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah and His Messenger.'" Rather, He made it purely His right, as He said: ﴿Indeed to Allah we turn in desire﴾ [al-Tawbah: 59], and He did not say "and to His Messenger," but made desire directed to Him alone, as He said: ﴿So when you are free, then labour; and to your Lord direct your longing﴾ [al-Sharh: 7-8]. So desire, reliance, turning in repentance, and sufficiency belong to Allah alone, just as worship, piety and prostration belong to Allah alone, and vowing and swearing are only to Him, the Glorified and Exalted. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ [al-Zumar: 36] (p-3032) So "hasb" is "kafi" (the one who suffices), and He, the Glorified and Exalted, informed that He alone suffices His servant. How then would He make His followers share with Allah in this sufficiency? The proofs demonstrating the invalidity of this corrupt interpretation are too many to mention here. End of quotation.

Al-Khafaji said in (al-'Inayah): His weakening of the nominative reading has no basis, for al-Farra' and al-Kisa'i preferred it, and what comes before and after it supports it. End of quotation.

I say: This is from al-Khafaji, from his fondness for argument, as is his habit. Had he reflected carefully on what Ibn al-Qayyim demonstrated and supported with such evidence that no doubt remains, he would not have weakened it. Al-Farra' and al-Kisa'i are scholars of the Arabic language, while the imams of interpretation have a different understanding, so reflect and do not be a captive of imitation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 65:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[65] ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers﴾ i.e., incite them: ﴿to fight. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are among you one hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you one thousand, they will overcome two thousand, by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the patient.﴾

**There are several issues in the verse:**

**The first:** It is legislated to urge people to fight and to exaggerate in exhorting them to it. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to rouse his companions when they lined up and faced the enemy, as when he said to them on the day of Badr, when the polytheists approached in their numbers and equipment: "Rise up to a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth." 'Umayr ibn al-Hammam said: "Its breadth is the heavens and the earth?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes!" He said: "Bakh, bakh!" He said: "What prompts you to say bakh, bakh?" He said: "Hoping that I may be among its people." He said: "Indeed you are among its people." So the man advanced, broke the sheath of his sword, took out some dates and began eating from them. Then he threw the rest of them from his hand and said: "If I live until I eat them, that is a long life!" Then he advanced and fought until he was killed, may Allah be pleased with him.

**The second:** Most scholars held that His saying, ﴿If there are among you twenty steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ [al-Anfal: 65], is a conditional in the sense of an order that it is obligatory for one to persevere against ten, i.e., that they not flee from them.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When ﴿If there are among you twenty steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ [al-Anfal: 65] was revealed, it was prescribed for them that not one of ten should flee, nor twenty from two hundred. Then ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you﴾ was revealed, and it was prescribed that not one hundred should flee from two hundred.

In another narration from him, he said: When ﴿If there are among you twenty steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ [al-Anfal: 65] was revealed, it was hard on the Muslims. Then ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you﴾ was revealed. When Allah lightened for them in number, He reduced for them in steadfastness by the same measure as He lightened.

In al-Lubab (Al-Lubab fi 'Ulum al-Kitab) it says: The apparent meaning is that His saying, ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you﴾, abrogates what came before in the first verse. This occurred on the day of Badr: Allah obligated one Muslim man to fight ten of the disbelievers, which was heavy upon the believers, so ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you﴾, O believers, was revealed, ﴿and He knows that there is weakness in you﴾, meaning in fighting one against ten. So if there are among you a hundred steadfast, seeking reward, they will overcome two hundred, and if there are a thousand, they will overcome two thousand, by the permission of Allah. Thus He reduced the ten to two. When the Muslims are at half the number of their enemy, it is not permissible for them to flee. Whoever flees from three without fleeing [from them]... and whoever flees from two has fled. End of quotation.

In al-Inayah it says: Makki (Makki ibn Abi Talib) held that it is a lightening and not an abrogation, like the lightening of breaking the fast for the traveler. The fruit of the disagreement is: if one fights ten and is killed, is he sinful or not? According to the first view he is sinful; according to the second he is not sinful.

Al-Razi said: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani (al-Isfahani) rejected the claim of abrogation in the verse, and said: The matter understood from the verse is conditioned on the twenty being able to persevere, i.e., if there arise among you twenty who are described as patient in confronting two hundred, then let them engage them.

Then His saying, ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you﴾, indicates that this condition was not met among them, so the obligation was not binding upon them.

In sum, the first verse establishes a ruling upon a specific condition, and the second indicates that this condition was absent in this group, so that ruling was not established. Thus there is no abrogation. Nor can it be said that His saying, ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you﴾, implies that this obligation was directed at them before it, for the word "lightening" does not necessarily indicate that there was a prior burden. The custom of the Arabs is to use such speech for concession, like His saying regarding His permission for the free man to marry a slave woman: ﴿Allah wishes to lighten [the burden] for you﴾ [al-Nisa: 28]. There is no abrogation there; rather, it is the permission to marry a slave woman for one who cannot afford free women. So it is likewise here.

**What indicates the absence of abrogation** is the mention of this verse alongside the first, and making the abrogating ruling contemporaneous with the abrogated, which is not permissible without a compelling proof.

Al-Razi said, after stating the words of Abu Muslim: If the consensus of the Ummah before Abu Muslim is established regarding the occurrence of abrogation in the verse, then there is nothing to say; otherwise, the view of Abu Muslim is sound and good. End of quotation.

**The third:** In His saying, ﴿because they are a people who do not comprehend﴾ [al-Anfal: 65], there is an indication of the reason for the believers' victory over ten times their number of disbelievers. The adverbial phrase is connected to "they will overcome" (yaghlibu), meaning: because they are people ignorant of Allah, the Exalted, and the Last Day, who do not fight seeking reward and in obedience to the command of Allah, the Exalted, and to exalt His word, and seeking His good pleasure, as the believers do. Rather, they fight only out of jahili (pre-Islamic) zeal, following the steps of Satan, and stirring up the flame of transgression and aggression. Thus they deserve nothing but subjugation and abandonment. This was conveyed by Abu al-Su'ud.

**The fourth:** Al-Razi said: Hisham argued in support of his view that Allah does not know particulars except when they occur, using His saying, ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you, and He knows that there is weakness in you﴾, since it implies that His knowledge of their weakness came about only at this time.

The theologians answered that its meaning is: Now the knowledge of its occurrence and existence has been attained. As for before that, what had been attained was the knowledge that it would occur or would come into being. End of quotation.

Al-Tibi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Its meaning: Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you, because the object of His knowledge has become manifest, i.e., your multitude which necessitates your weakness, after the manifestation of your killing and your strength.

**The fifth:** For "al-da'f" (weakness) there are two dialectal forms: with a fatha (al-fath) and with a damma (al-damm), and both have been read. This confirms that they carry the same meaning, so that it applies to both opinion and body. It is said that the fatha is used for opinion and intellect, and the damma for the body. This is transmitted from al-Khalil. It was also read as "du'afa'" in the plural form.

**The sixth:** If it is said: The sufficiency of twenty against two hundred suffices in place of the sufficiency of a hundred against a thousand, and the sufficiency of a hundred against two hundred suffices in place of the sufficiency of a thousand against two thousand, since it has been established that one must stand against ten in the first case and one against two in the second, what is the secret of this repetition?

I answer: Its secret is that each force is supported by the few against the many (p-3036), for the increase of repetition conveys greater assurance, and indicates that the situation regarding few and many is one and the same and does not vary. For twenty may not overcome two hundred, while a hundred may overcome a thousand. As for the order in the repeated statement, it is by mentioning the lesser and then the greater, in the natural order.

In al-Fath (Fath al-Bari) it says: It has been said regarding its secret that it is good news for the Muslims that the armies of Islam would exceed in number tens and hundreds, reaching thousands.

**The seventh:** In al-Bahr (al-Bahr al-Muhit) it says: Consider the eloquence of this speech. In the first conditional it mentioned the qualifier of patience and omitted its counterpart from the second. In the second it mentioned the qualifier of their being disbelievers and omitted it from the first. Since patience is highly desired, it was mentioned in both clauses of lightening and omitted from the second because the preceding clause indicates it. Then it was concluded with His saying, ﴿And Allah is with the patient﴾, as hyperbole regarding the intensity of its desirability. And in the two clauses of lightening, He did not bring the qualifier of disbelief, being content with what came before.

Al-Shihab said: This is a type of rhetorical embellishment (badi') called ihtibak (the omission of a counterpart that is understood from its parallel). It remains to note that ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾ was mentioned in the lightening clause, and it is a qualifier for both. His saying, ﴿And Allah is with the patient﴾, is an indication of their support, and that they will certainly be victorious, for whoever Allah is with cannot be overcome.

There remain in it subtle points. By Allah, how excellent is the sweetness of the water of its eloquence! And how bright is the radiance of its rhetoric!

The Explanation of His Words, may He be exalted:

[67] ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a massacre upon the land. You desire the goods of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter. And Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise.﴾

﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a massacre upon the land⁠﴾

Imam Ahmad narrated from Anas, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ consulted [his companions] about the captives on the day of Badr. He said: 'Indeed Allah has granted you power over them.' (p-3037) Then Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Strike their necks.' The Prophet ﷺ turned away from him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned to his statement and said: 'They are only your brothers of yesterday.' Umar repeated his statement, and he ﷺ turned away from him. Then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! We see that you should pardon them and accept ransom from them.' He said: So the distress that was upon the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed, and he pardoned them and accepted ransom from them."

Muslim included in his (Afrad) from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Abbas said: "When they took the captives, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Bakr and Umar: 'What do you think about these captives?' Abu Bakr said: 'O Messenger of Allah! They are the sons of our paternal uncles and our tribe. I see that you should take ransom from them, which will be a strength for us against the disbelievers, and perhaps Allah will guide them to Islam.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What do you see, O son of al-Khattab?' I said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah! I do not see what Abu Bakr sees. Rather I see that you should empower us so that we strike their necks, and empower Ali to [strike] Aqil's neck, and empower Hamza to [strike] al-Abbas's neck, and empower me over so-and-so, a relative of Umar, so that I strike his neck, for these are the leaders of disbelief and its chiefs.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ inclined to what Abu Bakr said, and did not incline to what I said.

When the next day came, I went, and behold, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr were weeping. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Tell me what you and your companion are weeping about, for if I find weeping I will weep, and if I do not find weeping I will feign weeping for your weeping.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'I weep over your companions for their taking ransom. Their punishment was presented to me, as near as this tree,'" for a tree near the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. "Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is not for a Prophet﴾ the verse."

Al-Humaydi mentioned it in his (Musnad) from Umar ibn al-Khattab, from the individual narrations of Muslim, with an addition in it.

The meaning of ﴿It is not for a Prophet﴾ is: it is not correct for him nor proper. It was read as (lil-nabiyyi) with the definite article, referring in either case to our Prophet ﷺ. It was stated in indefinite form (nabiyyin) out of gentleness toward him, so that he would not be confronted with punishment. It was also read as (Usara).

The meaning of ﴿inflicts a massacre upon the land⁠﴾ is: he increases killing and goes to excess in it, until disbelief is humbled, its party is diminished, Islam is honored, and its people gain dominion. It is said: "He inflicted (athkhana) upon the enemy," meaning he exceeded in reducing them. As in (al-Asas): "He inflicted upon the land killing" when he went to excess. Ibn al-A'rabi said: athkhana means he prevailed and subdued.

Al-Razi said: Most scholars understood it as killing, because a state only grows strong through it.

Al-Mutanabbi said:

"The lofty nobility is not free from harm until blood is spilled on its sides."

It also produces strength of awe and intensity of dread, which is why the Exalted commanded it. His words, may He be exalted, ﴿You desire the goods of this world⁠﴾ means its passing possessions, through the ransom of the captives of Badr.

Al-ʿaraḍ (ʿaraḍ) is that which has no permanence even if it is a body; from it the theologians borrowed "ʿaraḍ," the counterpart of "jawhar" (substance), as al-Shihab stated.

﴿But Allah desires the Hereafter⁠﴾ meaning: He desires its reward for you. ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might⁠﴾ meaning: Dominant over what He wills.

﴿Wise⁠﴾ meaning: in what He commands His servants.

The discussion of the words of God, Exalted is He:

[68] ﴿Had it not been for a decree from God that had already gone forth, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took.﴾

﴿Had it not been for a decree from God that had already gone forth, it would have touched you﴾, i.e., it would have befallen you; ﴿for what you took﴾, i.e., because of it, namely the ransom; ﴿a great punishment﴾, i.e., severe, in proportion to your nullifying the great wisdom, which is their killing, which is more honourable for Islam, more awe-inspiring to those behind them, and more weakening to their power. By "the Book" is meant the judgement, and it was called that because it is written in the Preserved Tablet.

The scholars of tafsir have several opinions concerning its interpretation. It was said: it means that He does not punish a people except after a prohibition has been given beforehand, and no prohibition concerning this had preceded it. It was said: it means that He does not punish one who errs in his ijtihad (independent judgement). It was said: it means the fact that the people of Badr were forgiven. And it was said: it means the permissibility of the spoils of war.

Al-Razi raised objections to these opinions, and he chose that "the Book" is His judgement from eternity to pardon this incident, because He has prescribed mercy upon Himself, and His mercy has preceded His wrath.

(p-3039) I say: Perhaps the most fitting interpretation, in magnifying what they had earned, is to explain "the Book" by what is in the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿But God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ [al-Anfal: 33]. And God knows best.

Notes:

The first: al-Razi said: Ibn 'Abbas said: this ruling applied only on the day of Badr, because the Muslims were few; then, when they increased and their authority grew, God revealed after that concerning the captives: ﴿Then either set them free as a favour or ransom them until the war lays down its burdens﴾ [Muhammad: 4].

I say: this statement gives the impression that His words ﴿then either set them free as a favour or ransom them﴾ [Muhammad: 4] intend the ruling of the verse we are interpreting, and this is not so, because the two verses are in agreement, for both indicate that there must be a prior subduing (ithkhan) of the enemy, and only after it the taking of ransom. End.

Some have said: the claim of abrogation (naskh) does not hold at its root, since the implicit prohibition, as here, is restricted and limited by the subduing, meaning that the great amount of fighting which is necessary for it is the strength and might of Islam; and what is in Surat al-Qital regarding the option belongs after the manifestation of the power of Islam through much fighting. So there is no contradiction between the two verses, since what is there is an explanation of the limit that is here. Transmitted by him in al-Fath.

The second: al-Qadi said: in the verse there is evidence that the prophets, peace be upon them, exercised ijtihad, and that it may be an error, but they are not left to persist in it.

The third: Ibn Kathir said: the ruling concerning captives has remained, according to the majority of scholars, that the Imam has the choice regarding them: if he wishes, he may kill them, as he did with the Banu Qurayzah; and if he wishes, he may free them in exchange for property, as he did with the captives of Badr; and if he wishes, he may enslave those who were captured. This is the position of Imam al-Shafi'i and a group. There is another disagreement among the imams on this question, established in its proper place.

(p-3040) The fourth: some of the commentators of the Zaydiyyah said: in this verse there is a question, which is: if their action was ijtihad and error, why were they rebuked? And it would follow that there was no disobedience. And if they were able to acquire knowledge and fell short, how did the Messenger ﷺ approve them? The answer to this is in two respects:

The first: from Abu 'Ali, that this was a minor disobedience. Al-Hakim said: and they were able to acquire knowledge when he rebuked them.

It was said: it was an error, and they fell short, so they were rebuked for the shortfall. End.

And the words of God, Exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 69:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[69] ﴿So eat of what you have taken as booty, lawful and good; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿So eat of what you have taken as booty, lawful and good﴾ — i.e., eat some of it after the khums (one-fifth) has been set aside, [as] lawful, meaning unrestricted from reproach and punishment, from (ḥall al-ʿiqāl, "the untying of the hobble").

﴿Good﴾ — i.e., pleasant and wholesome; or lawful by the Shariah, good by nature.

It has been said: this command is a confirmation of the lawfulness of the spoils, because it was already known from what preceded it, His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you take as booty﴾ [al-Anfal: 41], and as an indication that the ransom wealth is included in its generality. So "what you have taken as booty" here is either the ransom (fidyah), because it is booty, or the spoils in general.

The purpose is to explain the ruling on what is included within it of the ransom. The fa' (فَ) is taken as conjunctive, connected to an implied cause, i.e., "I have permitted you the spoils, so eat"; the "so eat" may be dispensed with by its connection to what precedes it in meaning, i.e., "I will not hold you accountable for what was taken as ransom, so eat it." Thus in (al-ʿInayah).

Abu al-Suʿud said: The more apparent view is that it is for conjunction with an implied element demanded by the context, i.e., "Leave it, so eat of what you have taken as booty." Then he said: It has been said that "what" (mā) refers to the ransom, since it is among the spoils, but the coherence and context of the noble composition reject this. End of quote. And this is well-reasoned.

﴿And fear Allah﴾ — i.e., in opposing His command and His prohibition. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — so He will forgive you and have mercy upon you if you fear Him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 70:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[70] ﴿O Prophet, say to those among the captives who are in your hands: If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you, and He will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿O Prophet, say to those among the captives who are in your hands﴾ That is, those who are in your possession, as if your hands were gripping them. This is for their deliverance from the captivity of misguidance through their weak faith. ﴿If Allah knows any good in your hearts﴾ That is, strength of faith and sincerity in it. ﴿He will give you better than what was taken from you﴾ That is, better than the ransom. Either He will replace it for you many times over in this world, or He will reward you in the Hereafter. ﴿And He will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[71] ﴿And if they intend to betray you, they have already betrayed God before, so He gave you power over them. And God is Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿And if they intend﴾ — i.e., the captives — ﴿to betray you﴾ — i.e., breaking what they pledged to you of Islam by apostasy, or withholding what they guaranteed of ransom. ﴿They have already betrayed God before﴾ — i.e., before (Badr) by disbelieving in Him.

﴿So He gave you power over them﴾ — i.e., He enabled you against them, that is, granted you victory over them by killing and capturing, as you saw on the day of Badr; so He will empower [you] over them if they return to betrayal. ﴿And God is Knowing and Wise﴾ — i.e., Knowing of what is in their inner selves of faith and assent, or treachery and breach of covenant; Wise, who recompenses each according to His knowledge: good with reward, and evil with punishment.

Ibn Hisham narrated in (al-Sirah) that the ransom of the polytheists on the day of Badr was four thousand dirhams per man, down to one thousand dirhams, except for those who had nothing, who were released by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) freely.

Ibn Ishaq said: The greatest ransom paid on the day of Badr was that of al-Abbas, because he was a wealthy man, and he ransomed himself for one hundred uqiyyas of gold.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Anas: "Some men of the Ansar said: 'O Messenger of God! Permit us to leave the ransom of our nephew al-Abbas.' He said: 'No, by God! You will not leave a single dirham of it.'"

Ibn Ishaq narrated: "Al-Abbas said: 'O Messenger of God! I was indeed a Muslim.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'God knows your Islam. If it is as you say, then God will reward you. But as for your outward conduct, it was against us. So ransom yourself, and your two nephews Nawfal and Aqil, and your ally Utbah.' He said: 'That is not with me, O Messenger of God!' He said: 'Then where is the wealth which you and Umm al-Fadl buried, and you said to her: If I am struck during this journey of mine, then this wealth is for my sons: al-Fadl, Abdullah and Qutham?' He said: 'By God! O Messenger of God, I know indeed that you are the Messenger of God; this is something no one knew except me and Umm al-Fadl. So reckon for me, O Messenger of God, what you have taken from me of twenty uqiyyas of wealth which was with me.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'No, that is something God the Exalted has given us from you.'"

So he ransomed himself, and his two nephews and his ally. God the Mighty and Majestic then revealed concerning him: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives﴾ [al-Anfal: 70], to the end of the verse.

Al-Abbas said: "God has given me in Islam, in place of the twenty uqiyyas, twenty slaves, each of whom has wealth in his hand that he trades with, along with what I hope of the forgiveness of God the Mighty and Majestic."

Ibn Ishaq also narrated that al-Abbas used to say: "By God, it was concerning me that it was revealed, when I mentioned my Islam to the Messenger of God (ﷺ)."

Ibn Jurayj narrated, on the authority of Ata' ibn Abi Rabah [note: as given, "Ata' ibn 'Abbas"], that "al-Abbas and his companions said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'We believe in what you have brought, and we testify that you are the Messenger of God; we will indeed advise you concerning our people.' So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿If God knows in your hearts﴾ [al-Anfal: 70], to the end of the verse." He said: "Al-Abbas used to say: 'I would not love that this verse had not been revealed concerning us, and that I had the world. He said: ﴿will give you better than what was taken from you﴾ [al-Anfal: 70], and He has given me better than what was taken from me a hundredfold. And He said: ﴿and will forgive you﴾ [al-Anfal: 70], and I hope that He has forgiven me.'"

Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: "Wealth was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from Bahrain, and he said: 'Scatter it in my mosque.' He said, and it was the largest amount ever brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He went out to the prayer and did not turn to them. When he had finished the prayer, he came and sat down by it, and he did not see anyone except that he gave to him. Then al-Abbas came to him and said: 'O Messenger of God! Give me, for I ransomed myself and I ransomed Aqil.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Take.' So he scooped it into his garment, then went to lift it, but he could not. He said: 'Tell someone to lift it for me onto me.' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then lift it yourself onto me.' He said: 'No!' So he shook out some of it, then hoisted it onto his shoulder and set off. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) kept following him with his eyes until he was out of sight, marvelling at his greed."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not rise until not a single dirham of it remained. In another narration: "He did not send a single dirham to his family." Al-Bukhari narrated it in suspended form (ta'liq).

In another narration: al-Abbas began saying as he was departing: "As for one of the two promises God made us, we have been given it; but we do not know what He will do with the other!"

Then He, exalted is He, mentioned the categories of believers and divided them into Emigrants and Helpers, saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 8, verse 72:

(p-3044) The discussion of the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[72] ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped – those are allies of one another. And those who believed but did not emigrate – you have no obligation of allegiance to them until they emigrate. And if they seek your help in matters of religion, then you must help, except against a people between yourselves and whom there is a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated﴾ – that is, from Makkah to al-Madinah, for the victory of Allah and His Messenger – ﴿and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾ – that is, in His obedience – ﴿and those who sheltered and helped﴾ – that is, they settled the emigrants, lodged them in their own dwellings, expended their wealth upon them, preferred them over themselves, and helped them against their enemies – ﴿those are allies of one another﴾ – that is, some of them take charge of others in support and backing, and one stands in the place of his own family and self, and he is more entitled to him than anyone. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established brotherhood (mu'akhah) between the emigrants and the Helpers.

Ibn Ishaq said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established brotherhood among his Companions, from among the emigrants and the Helpers, and he said, as it has reached us: 'Make brotherhood in pairs, two by two.' Then he took the hand of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and said: 'This is my brother.'" Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger, and the uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ), and Zayd ibn Harithah, the freedman of the Prophet (ﷺ), were brothers. It was to him that Hamzah bequeathed on the Day of (Uhud), when the fighting came upon him, in case the event of death befell him.

Ja'far, the one with two wings, the flier in Paradise, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal were brothers; Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Kharijah ibn Zayd were brothers; ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and ʿItban ibn Malik were brothers; Abu ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrah and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh were brothers; ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf and Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' were brothers; al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam and Salamah (p-3045) ibn Salamah were brothers; ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan and Aws ibn Thabit were brothers; Talhah ibn ʿUbayd Allah and Kaʿb ibn Malik were brothers; Sa'id ibn Zayd and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb were brothers; Mus'ab ibn ʿUmayr and Abu Ayyub al-Ansari were brothers; Abu Hudhayfah and ʿAbbad ibn Bishr were brothers; ʿAmmar ibn Yasir and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman were brothers; Abu Dhar al-Ghifari and al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr were brothers; Salman al-Farisi and Abu al-Darda' were brothers; Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah and ʿUwaym ibn Sa'idah were brothers; Bilal al-Habashi and Abu Ruwayhah al-Khath'ami were brothers.

When Bilal went out to al-Sham and stayed there fighting in the cause of Allah, ʿUmar said to him: "With whom shall we place your register?" He said: "With Abu Ruwayhah; I will never part from him, because of the brotherhood which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had established between him and me." So he was joined to him, and the register of the Abyssinians was joined to Khath'am, on account of Bilal's standing among them.

Ibn Ishaq said: These are the ones whom he named for us from among his Companions whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made brothers.

Note:

al-Wahidi reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and others that the intended meaning of this allegiance (wilayah) is the allegiance in inheritance. Ibn Kathir said: When they made brotherhood, they used to inherit from one another by that, a share given priority over kinship, until Allah abrogated that by the (general) inheritance laws. This is established in Sahih al-Bukhari from Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others.

al-Khafaji said: The emigrant would inherit from his Ansari brother if he had no emigrant guardian in Madinah, and there was no inheritance between him and his non-emigrant Muslim relative. This situation continued until the conquest of Makkah; afterwards they inherited by lineage, since there was no more emigration.

The walī is the close one and the helper, because its root meaning is physical nearness, and then it was applied to the figurative sense, such as lineage, religion and support.

At the beginning of Islam, the Prophet (ﷺ) made religious support into brotherhood, and gave it the legal effects of true brotherhood, including inheritance. So there is no basis for what is said, that this interpretation is not supported by the language; for allegiance on this reading is the inheritance arising from wisdom-based kinship. End.
